    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that financial software firm Intuit Inc.
    • Coming five years after Intuit agreed to acquire Mailchimp for $12 billion, the sale price is less than a third of what the company paid.
    • Although Bending Spoons describes the transaction as all-cash, Intuit will reinvest $368 million of its proceeds in newly issued Bending Spoons shares.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 17:17 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

    It has been revealed that financial software firm Intuit Inc. today declared that it has agreed to sell its Mailchimp email marketing business to Italian technology holding company Bending Spoons S.p.A. for about $3.68 billion.

    Coming five years after Intuit agreed to acquire Mailchimp for $12 billion, the sale price is less than a third of what the company paid. The 2021 purchase was the largest in Intuit’s history at the time.

    Although Bending Spoons describes the transaction as all-cash, Intuit will reinvest $368 million of its proceeds in newly issued Bending Spoons shares. That leaves Intuit with $3.31 billion in cash from the sale, according to the companies. Included in the deal is The Rocket Science Group LLC, the legal entity behind Mailchimp. Closing is expected in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

    Industry observers note that selling Mailchimp is said to sharpen Intuit’s focus on the artificial intelligence-native tools it has built to help businesses win fresh customers, manage their pipeline and grow. Once the deal closes, Intuit intends to use the cash proceeds to buy back its own shares before the end of fiscal 2027.

    Jack Tam, a senior vice president at Intuit, noted the manufacturer is confident Bending Spoons “will lead Mailchimp to continued success in this next chapter.”.

    Growth at Mailchimp has stalled in recent quarters. Revenue from the business fell 1% to $313 million in the quarter ended Oct. 31. Intuit’s full-year guidance has Mailchimp revenue coming in flat to down 1%. In November 2024, Chief Financial Officer Sandeep Aujla told analysts that Intuit was seeing higher churn from smaller Mailchimp customers.

    In a recent development, “Mailchimp is a powerful brand, built over two decades of reshaping the email marketing category and redefining how companies grow their audiences,” said Luca Ferrari, co-founder and chief executive of Bending Spoons. “We’re honored to welcome it to Bending Spoons and excited about what we can accomplish together.”.

    Industry observers note that ferrari added that Bending Spoons plans to invest substantially in Mailchimp after closing. According to Bending Spoons, the transformation of a business it acquires is typically deep, entailing reorganized teams, overhauled technology and redesigned user interfaces.

    Founded in 2013, Bending Spoons has built a portfolio of digital businesses that includes AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Tractive, Vimeo and WeTransfer. Since listing on the Nasdaq in July, the company has also completed acquisitions of Airtable Inc. for $1.285 billion and whiteboard platform Miro for $1.355 billion.

    It has been revealed that intuit declared the sale alongside its fiscal 2027 first-quarter results. For the quarter, it reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.91, up 56% from $1.87 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $4.35 billion, up 12% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting adjusted earnings of $2.70 per share on revenue of $4.31 billion.

    In a recent development, for its fiscal second quarter, Intuit expects adjusted earnings per share of $3.17 to $3.22 on revenue of $4.93 billion to $4.95 billion. Intuit lowered its full-year revenue guidance to between $23.08 billion and $23.37 billion.

    Sources indicate that behind the cut is Credit Karma, the tech giant’s personal finance and credit score service, which is now forecast to grow 3% to 7% this fiscal year, down from 11% to 13% previously. Intuit reiterated its full-year adjusted earnings guidance of $22.88 to $23.12 per share. None of the guidance includes the effect of the Mailchimp sale.

    Intuit shares fell more than 10% in after-hours trading.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.
    • People are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that.
    • An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.

    People are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that. Can AI help you find award flights and secure upgrades? It’s something I’d like to study in a bit more detail and write about in the coming weeks, but I just saw a post on Instagram that piqued my interest, so I figured it would make for a fun story. Consider this just a little teaser, for the time being.

    An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface. The idea is simply that ChatGPT helped someone secure an upgrade through the standard means — it’s not like ChatGPT used his/her/their charm to sweet talk someone into an upgrade by dressing up nicely. 😉.

    Let me actually just quote the description of the video, which covers most of the content:.

    What happens when you ask ChatGPT to upgrade your flight to first class?

    I tried this on my flight in two weeks and it actually worked.

    According to recent reports, go to ChatGPT and switch from Chat to Work at the top. Start a new chat and give it your airline and confirmation code.

    Prompt 1:“Ask me every question you need about my credit cards, my miles, and my memberships, and map out every upgrade currency I own for this exact flight.”.

    ChatGPT indicates you that you’ve been sitting on upgrade power this whole time without even knowing it.

    Prompt 2:“Now look up my exact flight, check how empty the first class cabin is, and tell me every way I can get up there, ranked from free to cheapest.”.

    Sources indicate that prompt 3:“Now go get me the upgrade. Use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.”.

    ChatGPT opens its own browser, logs into your airline, and actually chases that seat for you while you sit back and do nothing.

    You can watch the video for yourself below.

    A post shared by Maverick Maltin | AI & ChatGPT (@mavgpt).

    I don’t want to suggest AI isn’t useful, but I’d say that the example given is actually very poor. First of all, let’s be clear about what’s actually going on here. He had booked a business class ticket on American from Los Angeles (LAX) to London (LHR), and then upgraded to first class.

    Now, in the first place, something isn’t fully accurate here:.

    Okay, maybe he edited the dates, or something, which is fine, and it’s besides the point, but as a detail oriented airline nerd, I couldn’t help but notice those things. Anyway, let’s assume this is all accurate:.

    Recent findings suggest that to me, this is kind of where AI falls flat, and it isn’t the correct way to use it. The prompt was reportedly to “use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.” This is where I get confused — you’d think that AI would be able to scour reviews online, and see that American first class isn’t (well, or wasn’t) really viewed as a product that’s worth the premium.

    It has been revealed that if AI were really providing useful advice here, it would’ve recommend waitlisting with the systemwide upgrade, and otherwise recommending the guy save his 70,000 miles, and use them for something else. While there are definitely some strong use cases for AI, I think this is actually a pretty poor showing of what it can do.

    By the way, keep in mind that under United’s updated contract of carriage, using AI to help service reservations is banned, and could potentially get your ticket canceled. Whether there’s any enforcement of that remains to be seen.

    While the thought of using AI to score an upgrade might sound great, don’t count on it actually getting you the best deal. An AI whiz claims he has the secret to using AI to upgrade to first class. All AI did was use the instant upgrade offer that was available directly on American’s website, and it didn’t even encourage him to skip the upgrade due to it not being worthwhile, or waitlisting the upgrade with a systemwide upgrade, which is objectively a much better deal than 70,000 miles.

    What do you make of this AI “assistance” for a first class upgrade?

    According to recent reports, house Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., hold a press conference in the Capitol after the House Democratic leadership elections on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.

    Jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no declared opponent, won decisively, 251-11. The margin suggests Jeffries will easily surpass the necessary 218 votes he will need on the House floor when the full chamber votes in January.

    “It's a high honor and a distinct privilege to stand before the American people today as a Democratic nominee to be the next Speaker of the United States House of Representatives,” Jeffries said at a press conference following the election.

    While Jeffries celebrates his win, he has continued to put an emphasis on unity before he faces what has been deemed the toughest job in Washington. Democrats’ massive majority will give him some margin for maneuvering as he balances the priorities of a complex caucus ranging from moderates to progressives.

    “Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other,” Jeffries responded when asked about the 11 defections and what they mean for the next Congress. “Fight MAGA extremism, and to get significant things done for the American people, and that is what we are going to accomplish together, beginning on January 3rd.”.

    Seven of the 11 members who intended to vote against Jeffries released a statement saying that conversations with leadership are still “ongoing” and that there is “work to be done,” but noting there has been “meaningful progress.” The seven included Reps.- elect Darializa Avilia Chavelier, D-N.Y., Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., Frederick Haynes, D-Texas, Melat Kiros, D-Colo., Donovan McKinney, D-Mich., Chris Rabb, D-Pa., and Claire Valdez, D-N.Y.

    “Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues,” they wrote. “We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations.”.

    Newly elected House Democrats will meet with former President Barack Obama Wednesday night, where party unity will also be a likely topic.

    “This is the beginning of a new bargain, a new politics where hard work is honored and where people's voice is paramount, and where we have more confidence in the future than nostalgia for the past,” House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., said at the press conference.

    Recent findings suggest that rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., who made history two decades ago as the nation’s first female speaker, arrived for the vote chanting “Hakeem Jeffries!”, reflecting party leaders’ desire to start the long morning of balloting on a positive note.

    Industry observers note that jeffries' nomination followed the election of current Democratic Caucus Vice Chairman Ted Lieu, D-Calif., to serve as the caucus chair in the next Congress. Separate votes followed Wednesday morning, keeping Jeffries' leadership team intact: Clark, as the newly introduced majority leader and Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., as majority whip.

    Sources indicate that at his news conference, Jeffries noted that Clark was also making history as the first woman ever to serve in the position. Aguilar will also be the first Latino to serve as majority whip.

    “We've been looking at people's talents, not a particular gender or race, and I think that's a good thing,” outgoing Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, D-Md., a former majority leader, told reporters ahead of the election.

    Sources indicate that “I think Hakeem Jeffries is going to be a good speaker,” Hoyer continued. “He has the confidence of the caucus, and he has a good leadership team that is close knit and very organized.”.

    Jeffries expressed confidence in the weeks leading up to his securing the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who had remarked they remained “undecided” ahead of the election.

    Pelosi was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to move forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

    Sources indicate that the entire leadership team will be tested despite their numerical advantage over Republicans by the same internal tensions facing Senate Democrats, where current Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., is being challenged for leadership of the majority by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md.

    Jeffries remarked Tuesday that the approach to the caucus vote mirrored the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who was best positioned to lead based on their “track record, experience and vision.”.

    Jeffries has already outlined some of his top priorities of his speakership such as a hefty healthcare agenda, immigration legislation, and a multitude of investigations into the Trump administration.

    He also signaled Wednesday another area where his party’s restive base is likely to close ranks: oversight.

    “House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones,” he said at his news conference.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Microsoft Corp.’s official Python package for its Agent Framework artificial intelligence agent toolkit was compromised earlier this week, as an attacker published two malicious versions to the Python Package Index that were designed to steal cloud and developer credentials.
    • In a recent development, the malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on Tuesday through Microsoft’s own publisher account, giving them the appearance of a routine patch to a package that sees close to 200,000 downloads a month.
    • Sources indicate that researchers at cloud security manufacturer Wiz Inc.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 17:44 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

    Microsoft Corp.’s official Python package for its Agent Framework artificial intelligence agent toolkit was compromised earlier this week, as an attacker published two malicious versions to the Python Package Index that were designed to steal cloud and developer credentials.

    In a recent development, the malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on Tuesday through Microsoft’s own publisher account, giving them the appearance of a routine patch to a package that sees close to 200,000 downloads a month. Both versions were pulled from PyPI within about an hour, but anyone who installed them in that window is at risk.

    Sources indicate that researchers at cloud security manufacturer Wiz Inc. have since found that the attacker appears to have gained publishing access using a client certificate and private key for Microsoft’s Engineering System Release Pipeline, an internal service the company uses to sign and publish packages. Address filtering on the service blocked the attacker’s first attempt from Amazon Web Services, according to Wiz, though the attacker was able to publish on a second try from Microsoft-owned address space.

    How the attacker obtained the credentials is not known. Microsoft had not responded to a request for comment from BleepingComputer as of Wednesday.

    Sources indicate that the researchers also observed part of the operation, as the attacker’s tooling was reporting its progress to the same public webhook it was using to collect stolen data. The tooling identified itself as Cairn, an open-source penetration-testing framework that uses AI.

    Sources indicate that the malware itself is delivered through a .pth file added to both releases, a type of file Python runs every time it starts, meaning the credential stealer runs even if the framework itself is never imported. The two versions also kept the genuine agent-framework-core 1.26.0 as a dependency, so the framework continued to work normally while the malware ran in the background.

    Sources indicate that once running, the malware collects secrets from environment variables and from other running processes, along with credential files for services such as Azure, npm, Git, Docker and Hugging Face. It also requests Azure managed identity tokens for 12 resources, according to application security company Endor Labs Inc., with the second version adding requests for GitHub Actions tokens. The stolen data is then compressed, encoded and sent to a webhook.site address controlled by the attacker.

    Researchers at malware tracking site OpenSourceMalware described the malware as a “focused credential and token stealer, not a remote access trojan,” noting that it does not install any persistence on infected systems.

    Recent findings suggest that wiz’s analysis suggests the number of victims may be small, though it covers only the 50 requests the attacker’s free webhook.site account retained. Of those, 17 represented only three unique successful thefts of victim data, with the rest coming from the attacker’s own machines and from sandbox and security vendor scanning.

    Recent findings suggest that the incident is not the first this year involving an official Microsoft Python package. In May, Microsoft’s durabletask package was hijacked after its PyPI token was stolen in an attack that has been linked to TeamPCP, the group also behind the compromise of LiteLLM. Wiz states it has not linked the two incidents.

    Anyone who installed either of the malicious versions is being urged to treat it as a credential compromise, according to researchers, who recommend rebuilding from version 1.26.0 and rotating any secrets the affected systems could access.

    “A list of dependencies in production might show no trace of the framework, while a build runner could have installed it and been shut down before the alert arrived,” James Matchett, head of security at software supply chain security company Cloudsmith Ltd., told SiliconANGLE.

    “If that runner had access to a deployment token, the team needs to know which version it installed and what the token could access,” he added.

    Resolve AI’s SRE-1 model finds root causes of production alerts as AI agents go on call

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that incident remediation tech giant Resolve AI Inc.
    • The upcoming model, announced Wednesday, reflects the organization’s argument that while AI has transformed how software gets written, it has barely touched how software gets run.
    • According to recent reports, SRE-1 is a 27 billion-parameter model built on open weights and trained by a team of 16 AI researchers over a final run of 7.4 days on up to 512 graphics processing units.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 18:11 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

    Industry observers note that incident remediation tech giant Resolve AI Inc. has revealed the launch of SRE-1, a new model that has been trained to find the root cause of production alerts, and Primary On-call, a new service that puts its artificial intelligence agents on call ahead of human engineers.

    The upcoming model, announced Wednesday, reflects the organization’s argument that while AI has transformed how software gets written, it has barely touched how software gets run. According to Resolve AI, production has no public training corpus to match the published code that models learned from, as incidents at each company stay private.

    According to recent reports, SRE-1 is a 27 billion-parameter model built on open weights and trained by a team of 16 AI researchers over a final run of 7.4 days on up to 512 graphics processing units. Measured on the same incidents before and after training, which used reinforcement learning alone, the pass rate for a single investigation rose from 6.9% to 38.8%.

    Recent findings suggest that resolve AI used Snowflake Inc.’s Cortex Training, a serverless service for customizing open-weight models, to build SRE-1. Snowflake Senior Vice President of Engineering Vivek Raghunathan said Resolve AI was the first design partner for the service.

    In a recent development, in testing on 49 difficult live production cases, each run five times, an ensemble of five SRE-1 investigations matched the strongest frontier model tested at a lower cost, according to the company. Resolve AI also benchmarked its complete system on 178 production alert investigations, solving about twice as many incidents as general-purpose coding agents.

    According to recent reports, primary On-call puts that research to work on the critical path. Each page is investigated across telemetry, infrastructure, code and operational knowledge, according to the tech giant. Depending on what it finds, the agent can close the alert, mitigate the problem where a team’s policies permit or escalate to a human. Once it has acted, the agent checks the fix against the production baseline, monitoring it until recovery holds.

    The agent also links related alerts and investigations into a shared view of each underlying problem. For teams wary of handing over the pager straight away, Resolve AI offers a shadow mode that records the call the agent would have made on each page.

    According to recent reports, up to 80% of paged alerts in production are noted to be handled by Primary On-call without escalation. Customers have reported a tenfold improvement in mean time to resolution, along with root-cause accuracy of up to 95%, according to Resolve AI.

    Salesforce Inc. is among the early users. Bhupesh Patel, a software engineering principal architect at Salesforce, stated that in the first few weeks of dark launch testing, the agent closed more than 70% of the CRM Analytics team’s paging alerts “without waking an engineer.”.

    It has been revealed that “No engineering team can keep up with how fast code and patches land in production,” remarked Resolve AI Chief Executive Spiros Xanthos. “The answer is agents that are accurate and fast enough to sit on the critical path, and that takes a model built for production.”.

    Primary On-call is now generally available. Access to SRE-1 is limited to Resolve AI’s own platform.

    Resolve AI is a venture capital-backed startup that has raised more than $190 million to date, including a $40 million extension to its Series A round in April, led by DST Global and Salesforce Ventures, that valued the manufacturer at $1.5 billion. Notable customers include Coinbase Global Inc., DoorDash Inc., Figma Inc., MSCI Inc., Nasdaq Inc., SAP SE and Zscaler Inc.

    In a recent development, the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® is American’s primary co-branded business credit card. We’re currently seeing an excellent limited time welcome offer, which is in line with the highest ever offer that we’ve seen on the card.

    That makes this the ideal time to apply for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. Not only that, but this is a card that many people will want, given that it’s my favorite American card for earning AAdvantage elite status, since you can basically double dip Loyalty Points.

    Link: Learn more about the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard®.

    The Citi AAdvantage Business Card right now has a limited time welcome offer of 75,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $5,000 within the first five months. This is a highest-ever offer, in line with the best bonuses I recall seeing on the card (I covered the card’s offer history below). We don’t know when this offer will be pulled.

    Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I value AAdvantage miles at 1.5 cents each, so to me the bonus is worth $1,125. There are some incredible uses of American AAdvantage miles, including for travel on some world class partner airlines.

    Just to give a few examples of AAdvantage mileage redemptions, you could redeem 57,500 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Finnair business class award from Dallas (DFW) to Helsinki (HEL)….

    …or you could redeem 60,000 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Japan Airlines business class award from Dallas (DFW) to Tokyo (HND)….

    …or you could redeem 40,000 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Etihad business class award (or 50,000 miles for an Etihad first class award) from Abu Dhabi (AUH) to Tokyo (NRT).

    In each case, these tickets would typically cost many thousands of dollars, so you’re getting incredible value. When there is award availability, AAdvantage really is a program that’s tough to beat.

    Also keep in mind that credit card spending will qualify for Loyalty Points (helping you earn elite status, including Gold, Platinum, Platinum Pro, or Executive Platinum), though the welcome bonus as such won’t. Upon completing minimum spending, you’d earn a minimum of 5,000 Loyalty Points. As I’ll explain below, you can even double dip the Loyalty Points you earn.

    The Citi AAdvantage Business Card 75,000-point offer is the best publicly available sign-up bonus that we’ve seen on the card. How do the previous Citi AAdvantage Business Card bonuses compare?

    As you can see, the Citi AAdvantage Business Card publicly available welcome offer has most commonly varied from 65,000 to 75,000 miles, so you might as well apply when the offer is the best.

    If you’re interested in applying for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, the typical Citi credit card application restrictions apply, including that you can be approved for at most one Citi card every eight days, and at most two Citi cards every 65 days.

    On top of that, the bonus isn’t available to those who have received a latest account bonus on this exact card in the past 48 months. Eligibility is unrelated to having any other American Airlines credit cards.

    It has been revealed that there’s not a published credit score you need to get approved for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. Ideally I’d hope to have a credit score of 700+, but people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been denied.

    Industry observers note that if you’re concerned about Chase’s 5/24 rule, note that applying for a Citi business card generally won’t count toward that limit. I should also mention that at least anecdotally, this card seems to be quite easy to get approved for.

    It has been revealed that the Citi AAdvantage Business Card has an annual fee that’s waived for the first year, so you can “try” the card before you have to pay a fee. While the fee after that is technically still $99, it’s increasing to $150 as of January 24, 2027, so that’s what you’d pay on account renewal. There’s no cost to add employee cards for authorized owners.

If you add an authorized user, their spending will earn 1x Loyalty Points per dollar spent for both their own account, and for the primary cardmember’s account. So this is a way to essentially get two-for-one elite status qualification, which is awesome.

    With the annual fee increasing as of January 2027, the card will also pick up several valuable new perks, including the following:.

    This is also my favorite card for earning AAdvantage elite status, since you can essentially earn Loyalty Points for two members at once. Authorized user spending earns Loyalty Points for the authorized user’s AAdvantage account, and also for the primary cardmember’s AAdvantage account.

    #145532. We Tracked The World’s Oldest Airbus A380 For A Week

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1512 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    We Tracked The World’s Oldest Airbus A380 For A Week

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1512 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that emirates is generally said to have the oldest Airbus A380-800 Superjumbo remaining in service today.
    • According to recent reports, in fact, by the time Emirates started operating the world's 'oldest' A380, Qantas had been flying three of its Superjumbos that remain in service today for months.
    • The Emirates Airbus A380 is the oldest commercial passenger Superjumbo still operating in the world as of the time of writing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that emirates is generally said to have the oldest Airbus A380-800 Superjumbo remaining in service today. While that is defensible when measured from MSN sequence and year of manufacture, it is not without its challengers. Airbus is (still) flying its first Superjumbo, built as a testbed, and Qantas' oldest A380s were delivered before Emirates' oldest aircraft.

    According to recent reports, in fact, by the time Emirates started operating the world's 'oldest' A380, Qantas had been flying three of its Superjumbos that remain in service today for months. To cover all bases, this article will provide the latest flight-tracking data for all three claimants to the world's oldest in-service Superjumbo accolade. Even if Emirates isn't deemed to have the oldest examples in service, it likely will in the next few years as other airlines phase out their A380s and Emirates doubles down on plans to operate them through the 2030s.

    The Emirates Airbus A380 is the oldest commercial passenger Superjumbo still operating in the world as of the time of writing. This is the oldest by year of manufacture. The aircraft (registered A6-EDF) bears MSN 007 and was built in 2006. The massive aircraft was delivered to Emirates in December 2009 but was later mothballed during COVID-19. The aircraft was pulled out of storage and returned to service in April 2025, five years later.

    Industry observers note that as suggested by its MSN, A6-EDF is far from the oldest A380 actually built. It is technically also not the oldest remaining in service (more about F-WWOW below). The older aircraft include the Airbus MSN 101 (F-WWOW) testbed, the Airbus MSN 002 prototype (now preserved at Toulouse), and the units with MSNs 003 through 006. Of those four older aircraft, two are scrapped, one is preserved at Le Bourget in Paris, and one is stored in Tarbes.

    The three examples are older than Emirates' A6-EDF, which flew for Singapore Airlines. It's also worth noting that all six of the next production aircraft (MSN 008 through MSN 013) are also scrapped, parked, or stored. The next oldest pair of Superjumbos in active commercial use are Qantas' VH-OQA and VH-OQB (MSN 014, MSN 015). The catch is that these aircraft were built later, but delivered sooner (in 2008).

    In a recent development, the date of writing is November 17, and so the last week stretches back to November 10 or 9, depending on how the dates are counted. Flight data for the 17th is not yet available. A6-EDF's most recent flight was the three-hour hop from Egypt's Cairo back to Dubai, returning from the same-day three-hour and 40-minute flight. Yesterday (16) was a busy day for the aircraft as it flew back from Bangkok to Dubai that morning (a six-hour flight).

    According to recent reports, starting at the beginning of the week (November 9), the aging A380 flew from Dubai to Mauritius and back again the same day as Flights EK702 and EK19, respectively. On the 10th, it flew from Dubai to Manchester and back. The next day, it flew to London and back, and then to Manchester and back the following day. On the 13th, it flew as EK362 to Guangzhou in China and returned as Flight EK363 the following day.

    Flight number (outbound/inbound).

    Flight duration (outbound/inbound).

    Arriving in the early hours of the morning, it took off for Cairo that evening, then returned in the early morning hours that night (the 15th). This set the stage for it to fly later on the 15th to Bangkok, before returning as mentioned above. Notably, none of these flights are ultra-long haul. The longest flight in the last week has been the eight-hour return flight from Guangzhou, although most flights have been between five and eight hours.

    Emirates entered 2026 planning to expand its active Airbus A380 fleet from around 95–96 aircraft to up to 110 by the end of the year. However, then Operation Epic Fury happened; Emirates was forced to grapple with all the flight disruptions, closed airspace, and higher fuel prices that came with it. As of October, Emirates' earlier strategy has been more or less inverted.

    Industry observers note that while Emirates still has a total of 116 A380s in inventory, only around 84 are in active service. 24 are listed as being parked or in reserve/maintenance, and the remaining seven are in long-term storage. Emirates President Sir Tim Clark has said that a major reason for the shortfall is engine overhaul bottlenecks, with contracted 85-day engine shop visits dragging on for over 350 days, as well as the airline's ongoing cabin retrofit program, which can ground them for up to a month.

    Sources indicate that making matters worse, the regional conflict has decreased passenger traffic, reducing the need for more capacity. High fuel costs have also been contributing to prioritizing more fuel-efficient twin-engined aircraft. Still, over the longer term, Emirates is doubling down on extending the A380's service, something more key with 777-9 delays. In October, Clark once again pitched his idea for an 'A380neo', promising to buy a minimum of 100 aircraft.

    Recent findings suggest that if the oldest A380 is defined as the one with the earliest delivery date to the airline, then Qantas can claim to have the oldest Airbus A380 Superjumbo flying today. VH-OQA (called Nancy-Bird Walton) was delivered in September 2008, over a year before the Emirates A380 discussed above. This is the aircraft that suffered an engine #2 failure after takeoff while en route to Sydney in November 2010.

    The aircraft lost part of its engine, but the crew managed to shut it down and safely land in Singapore after dumping fuel. The aircraft was returned to service in 2012 and later placed into storage during the pandemic. It returned to service in 2024. While Qantas claims to have the oldest commercial A380 flying, it won't keep it.

    In a recent development, in 2026, Qantas revealed it will bring forward the retirement of its Superjumbos by four years, starting in 2028. The decision is partly due to increased confidence in its pending A350-1000ULR deliveries. Regarding its name, Qantas wrote in 2008, "And on September 30 2008, in a very special ceremony, we named our first A380 after Nancy-Bird Walton – an inspiring Australian who overcame the same challenges as her peers, while overcoming the sexism of her times.".

    In a recent development, over the last week, VH-OQA has been dedicated to its Sydney to Los Angeles route, although it was also operating the Sydney to Dallas route the week before and the Sydney to Singapore route before that. In October, some of its flights took it all the way to London, via the refueling stopover in Singapore. In the last week, it has been operating as Flight QF11 outbound to Los Angeles and Flight QF12 inbound from Los Angeles.

    According to recent reports, these ultra-long-haul transpacific routes take between 13 hours and 13 hours and 30 minutes outbound and around 14 hours and 15 minutes return. All of Qantas' A380s are based in Sydney and fly flagship long-haul routes. The route to Dallas stands out, as it's better understood as a trunk route connecting to Qantas' partner, American Airlines' major hub, than as a destination.

    Qantas configures its Superjumbos with 14 first class seats, 70 business class seats, 60 premium economy seats, and 341 economy class seats. This gives the aircraft a total seat count of 485 seats. The primary aircraft set to replace the A380 in Qantas service is the fleet of 12 specially modified A350-1000ULRs being built for Qantas. These are to provide the range needed to directly link Sydney with London and New York without intermediate refueling stops.

    It should be noted that Emirates' A6-EDF is the oldest Superjumbo remaining in commercial passenger use, but it is not the oldest example of the A380 flying, and neither is the Qantas jet. That is the testbed aircraft Airbus operates, registered F-WWOW (MSN 001). F-WWOW is the first Superjumbo ever built, having made its maiden flight in April 2005, two years before the A380 entered commercial service.

    Recent findings suggest that F-WWOW remains active, although, as a testbed, its flying is patchy. Its most recent flight took place on October 28, 2026, from its base at Toulouse. It flew for one hour and 36 minutes before returning to Toulouse. It also flew on October 22 for two hours and 43 minutes. Before that, it flew twice in July, 17 times in June, three times in May, 11 times each in March and April, twice in February, and nothing before that since July 2025.

    But time is running out for the original A380. Airbus is in the process of replacing F-WWOW with a former Malaysia Airlines Airbus A380 (MSN 114). The aircraft, now registered as 2-JAYN, has been acquired by Airbus and has been in storage since 2020 after completing seven years of commercial service. It is unclear when F-WWOW will be permanently retired.

    Despite posting a solid earnings beat, Elastic sees its stock slide on rough guidance

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (972 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Elastic N.V.’s stock was trending lower in late trading today after the enterprise search software firm reported earnings and revenue that beat Wall Street’s expectations but disappointed with guidance that came in below forecasts.
    • Recent findings suggest that the firm reported second-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 94 cents per share, easily beating the analyst consensus estimate of 81 cents.
    • In a recent development, the results helped Elastic bounce back into profitability.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 18:33 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

    Elastic N.V.’s stock was trending lower in late trading today after the enterprise search software firm reported earnings and revenue that beat Wall Street’s expectations but disappointed with guidance that came in below forecasts.

    Recent findings suggest that the firm reported second-quarter earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 94 cents per share, easily beating the analyst consensus estimate of 81 cents. Revenue rose 17%, to $496 million, surpassing the Street’s target of $487 million.

    In a recent development, the results helped Elastic bounce back into profitability. Its net income for the quarter came to $171 million, rebounding from a loss of $51.3 million in the same period one year ago.

    In a recent development, however, investors were less than impressed with the organization’s guidance. For the quarter in progress, Elastic said it’s looking for earnings of between 90 cents and 92 cents per share on sales of $507.5 million to $508.5 million. That’s some way below the Street’s targets of 95 cents in earnings and $517.6 million in revenue. The company is not helped by the weak Euro, with currency conversions likely to cause a $4.5 million headwind on revenue in the quarter.

    The full-year picture is not much better, as Elastic forecast annual sales of between $2 billion and $2.01 billion compared with the Street’s model of $2.01 billion.

    Recent findings suggest that netherlands-based Elastic is one of Europe’s most successful software companies. It’s the developer of the popular open-source enterprise search platform Elasticsearch, which is used by thousands of businesses all over the world. The base platform is free to download and use, with Elastic making money by selling a special cloud-hosted version that ships with premium features not available in the open edition. The organization also sells application observability and security tools.

    Sources indicate that in the last couple of years, Elastic has tried to cash in on the artificial intelligence boom by positioning Elasticsearch as a useful cog in the wheel that feeds real-time data into large language models to provide them with business context. A key capability is Elastic Context Engine, which gathers, structures, and serves business-specific context to AI agents so they can make accurate decisions with fewer tokens and lower latency.

    More recently, the manufacturer has built AI-native products including AlertZero, which enables enterprises to orchestrate teams of autonomous security agents that automate tasks around data protection and threat hunting.

    Elastic Chief Executive Ash Kulkarni (pictured) said he’s excited about the potential of those fresh capabilities to drive significant revenue over time. “Elastic delivered another strong quarter, beating guidance across all key metrics,” he said. “Our strong results reflect expanding customer adoption and position us well to continue our strong execution in the back half of fiscal 2027.”.

    In a recent development, unfortunately for Kulkarni, investors didn’t seem to share his enthusiasm. The market was clearly expecting trouble on the horizon in the hours before the organization published its report, as its stock declined 8% during regular trading. Once the results were out, it fell another 8% after-hours. That means Elastic’s stock is now up just over 1% in the year to date.

    Elastic’s stock had rallied more than 150% between April and October, but virtually all of those gains have now been erased. Prior to today, the shares had already lost more than 20% this month amid broader concerns about the AI industry. Some investors continue to worry about the potential of AI technology to challenge the business models of software companies.

    Elastic is trying to sidestep those concerns by de-emphasizing search and observability and moving towards runtime context, model evaluation and AI operations, but investors are not yet convinced it will be able to do so successfully, Constellation Research analyst Michael Ni told SiliconANGLE.

    “While Elastic is showing good underlying momentum, the Street wants to see more proof that its re-acceleration can hold,” Ni said. “The next few quarters will show whether the broader platform story translates into sustainable growth or remains ahead of the numbers.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Google LLC today released a new version of Gemini’s Mac client that can interact with other apps on the user’s computer.
    • Recent findings suggest that the feature is available in the U.S.
    • People can instruct Gemini to launch a local app by including the command “@Computer use” in their prompts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 18:41 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

    Google LLC today released a new version of Gemini’s Mac client that can interact with other apps on the user’s computer.

    Recent findings suggest that the feature is available in the U.S. on launch. It requires a Google AI subscription, which equips consumer Google accounts with a broader lineup of artificial intelligence tools. The offering also includes additional storage space and certain other features.

    People can instruct Gemini to launch a local app by including the command “@Computer use” in their prompts. For example, a designer could upload a sketch of a vehicle and ask the AI assistant to turn it into a three-dimensional animation. Gemini finds the local app that is needed for the task, creates a project plan and carries out the work step by step.

    According to recent reports, the assistant supports tasks that comprise dozens of actions. Furthermore, consumers can use the output of a newly completed Gemini workflow to launch follow-up projects. A user could have the assistant generate a visual asset in a design tool and then turn it into a mini-app with Visual Studio Code.

    Gemini can interact with not only local apps but also web services. That means it can load data from webpages into programs that run on the user’s machine, as well as move data in the opposite direction and between cloud services.

    The AI carries out its work in a background window. As a result, users don’t have to pause their work while the assistant is running. They can track Gemini workflows via a preview pane built into the Mac client’s chat window. Additionally, Google has included controls that make it possible to give Gemini feedback mid-task.

    “Privacy and safety are built in: you choose which apps Gemini can access, watch every step live, pause at any time, and approve key actions before they happen,” Michael Friedman, Google’s group product manager for the Gemini app, wrote in a blog post.

    According to recent reports, the Mac version of Muse, Meta Platforms Inc.’s recently launched AI agent, can also interact with local apps and data. Furthermore, a cloud-based virtual machine enables it to perform tasks even when the user’s computer is offline. Dots, a competing service from OpenAI Group PBC, offers a similar capability.

    Sources indicate that google may seek to match its rivals’ cloud-based workflow hosting features in the future. The tech giant can also extend Gemini in other ways. Notably, it could bring Gemini’s computer use mode to additional operating systems and add features for business people. OpenAI’s Dots already includes capabilities designed to automate business workflows such as procurement.

    Before I get into my Atmos Rewards Business Card review, here’s a brief summary of the key details of the card:.

    Below are what I consider to be the pros and cons of the Atmos Rewards Business Card.

    Industry observers note that the Atmos Rewards Business Card is the only business card in the Atmos Rewards ecosystem. To start, let’s cover the welcome bonus, card eligibility rules, annual fee, and more, since these are notable factors that cardmembers consider.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus where you’ll get 90,000 bonus points after you make $6,000 or more in purchases within the first 90 days of opening your account. The good news is that eligibility for this card is unrelated to having any other Atmos Rewards card, so you’re eligible for this card (including the bonus) if you have the Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card (learn more) or Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more).

    Let me emphasize that you are eligible for this product if you have any of the previously issued personal or business HawaiianMiles Barclays cards, or any of the previously issued personal Alaska Mileage Proposal cards.

    In a recent development, beyond that, Bank of America doesn’t have many consistent restrictions when it comes to getting approved for business cards. While Bank of America has the 2/3/4 rule and 3/12 rules, those apply to personal cards, and not business cards. Generally those with a Bank of America banking relationship also have the best odds of approval (though it’s by no means a requirement).

    There’s not a consistent credit score you need to have to be approved for this card, though personally I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

    Applying for this card won’t count as a further card toward Chase’s 5/24 limit, in case that’s a limit you’re trying to stay under.

    Sources indicate that on the surface, this suggests you may be declined for a Bank of America business card if you have another Bank of America business card. However, anecdotally, this doesn’t appear to be enforced much. I think the term “may” is the key here (which is different than “will”).

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card has bonus categories that can help you rack up points faster. Furthermore, spending on the card can help you earn Atmos Rewards elite status. Let’s talk about how rewarding spending on the card can be.

    It has been revealed that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 10x points per dollar spent on flights booked through the Atmos for Business website. If you’re looking to maximize your earning, this is where you want to book your Alaska and Hawaiian flights, as this is an incredible deal.

    Industry observers note that you do need your own business to participate in the Atmos for Business program, and once registered, the return on spending is really tough to beat. Based on my valuation of points, that’s like an incremental 15% return on eligible airfare spending, on top of what you otherwise earn.

    Industry observers note that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 3x points on all other eligible Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, with no caps. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 4.5% return on spending. So if you fly either of those Alaska Air Group carriers with any frequency, that’s a solid return on that spending.

    Sources indicate that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 2x points on eligible dining purchases. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 1.5% return on spending. It’s always nice to earn bonus points, though in fairness, 2x points isn’t exactly the biggest return on spending that we’ve seen.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 1x points on all other eligible spending. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 1.5% return on spending. As you might expect, there are more exciting cards for everyday spending, as independently, that’s not a terribly exciting return.

    In a recent development, the Atmos Rewards Business Card can help you earn elite status in the Atmos Rewards program. Specifically, the card offers one status point for every $3 in eligible spending. There’s no cap on how many status points you can earn with the card.

    Beyond the ability to earn one status point per $3 spent, the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers some additional threshold bonuses for spending, including bonus status points and discount codes:.

    It has been revealed that in other words, spending $200,000 per anniversary year would earn you 20,000 bonus status points, plus a discount code for 50% off a base fare. Just to cover the basics of that 50% off base fare discount code, here’s how that works:.

    Recent findings suggest that so the value of this will depend on how you’d usually travel, but this could easily save you many hundreds of dollars, depending on the type of ticket you book. It’s also still possible to upgrade these tickets, but at least the initial booking has to be in economy.

    In a recent development, the Atmos Rewards Business Card also offers a Bank of America relationship bonus. If you have an eligible small business Bank of America checking or savings account, you’ll receive a bonus equal to 10% of the points you earn on each dollar spent.

    This is a way to earn even more rewards, as you’d earn 11x points on Atmos for Business purchases, 3.3x points on Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, 2.2x points on the other purchases eligible for bonus categories, and 1.1x points on everyday spending.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a decent card to use for purchases abroad, since you can rack up rewards without paying a fee.

    According to recent reports, the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers a variety of benefits and credits, which can potentially more than justify the annual fee year after year. These perks are the main reason you want to consider picking up this card, in addition to the great welcome bonus. In no particular order, let’s go over the main benefits.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers a free checked bag for you and up to six guests on the same reservation when flying on Alaska or Hawaiian. In order to be eligible for this perk, you need to charge the cost of the ticket to your card. Another great thing is that authorized people on the card can also receive this benefit, as long as their ticket is purchased with the card, so that’s a huge incentive to add authorized users to the card.

    It has been revealed that this is a great benefit that could save you a lot of money — Alaska and Hawaiian ordinarily charge $30-45 per checked bag, so that’s a savings of up to $90 per person roundtrip, if checking bags. If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian fairly often but don’t have elite status, that alone could rapidly more than justify the annual fee.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers preferred boarding for you and up to six guests on the same reservation. In order to be eligible for this perk, you need to charge the cost of the ticket to your card. Another great thing is that authorized users on the card can also receive this benefit, as long as their ticket is purchased with the card.

    This is a valuable benefit that helps you ensure that there’s space in the overhead bin for your bags. It’s also an awesome authorized user perk, so that you can share this benefit with others.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers four Alaska Lounge passes annually. The way this works, the primary cardmember will have one Alaska Lounge pass deposited into their Atmos Rewards account at the beginning of the quarter, valid through the end of the quarter.

    Each is valid for access to Alaska Lounges on a single calendar day, in conjunction with a same day flight operated by Alaska, Hawaiian, a oneworld airline, or an Alaska global partner. Each pass is valid for one adult, plus accompanying children. For what it’s worth, a day pass would otherwise cost $60 per person.

    If you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you can share your Atmos Rewards points with other members at no cost. The way this works, you can link your accounts with up to 10 other Atmos Rewards members (they don’t have to be family — accounts of friends are fine as well), and then you can move points back and forth for free.

    I’d argue that this is especially compelling for families, because it’s easier to rack up a sizable balance of points when you can consolidate them into one account.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 20% back on Alaska and Hawaiian inflight purchases when paying with your card. This applies for the purchase of food, beverages, and Wi-Fi onboard flights, and the statement credit should post to your account within seven days. There’s no limit to how often you can take advantage of this.

    According to recent reports, let me just mention that Alaska and Hawaiian should have free Starlink Wi-Fi fleetwide by some point in 2027, at which point there won’t be savings anymore with Wi-Fi. That being mentioned, it can still be used for food and beverages.

    If you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, then you’re eligible for a free same day confirmed flight change on Alaska. This ordinarily costs $50 per person, so that’s quite valuable.

    With this, you can change to another flight that might be more convenient, subject to capacity controls. This is especially useful in high frequency markets.

    If you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you’re eligible to receive a $50 voucher if you have an Alaska flight that is delayed by at least two hours, or that’s canceled within 24 hours of departure.

    Industry observers note that the $50 voucher is valid for 48 hours, and will be delivered to the email address associated with the reservation, and can be used for food, drinks, etc. Travel must have been booked directly with Alaska using the eligible credit card.

    Those with the Atmos Rewards Business Card receive up to a $120 airport security credit every four years, in connection with TSA PreCheck or Global Entry. This is a perk offered by many premium credit cards, and there’s lots of value to this.

    It has been revealed that when talking about an Atmos Rewards credit card, it’s worth acknowledging the general value in earning and redeeming Atmos Rewards points. Alaska & Hawaiian are both in the oneworld alliance, and Atmos Rewards partners not only with oneworld partner airlines, but also with all kinds of other unaligned airlines. I consider Atmos Rewards to be one of the most valuable points currencies out there.

    It has been revealed that atmos Rewards has a distance based award chart, which varies a bit by region. For example, below is the one-way award chart within the Americas.

    I constantly redeem Atmos Rewards points for travel within the United States, particularly on American. For example, all the time I redeem 4,500 points to fly one-way economy from Miami to Tampa (when cash fares would often be $200+), or 15,000 points to fly one-way business class from Miami to Chicago or New York (when cash fares would often be $500+). You simply can’t beat these redemption rates.

    The icing on the cake is that with Atmos Rewards, you earn status points for award flights, so those flights even count toward elite status, and that’s also why I’ve switched my business to Atmos Rewards.

    According to recent reports, of course there are lots of other opportunities with Atmos Rewards points as well. For example, I love the ability to redeem 75,000 points for one-way business class from the United States to many parts of Asia on carriers like Japan Airlines or Starlux Airlines — those are both awards that I’ve booked for myself in the past, and they were a great value.

    What makes this an even better value is that you can have a free stopover on a one-way award when traveling long haul. One thing worth being aware of is that Atmos Rewards has a $20 per person per direction partner award booking fee. However, that can be waived if you have the Atmos Rewards Summit Card.

    According to recent reports, the Atmos Rewards Business Card is the only business card in the Atmos Rewards ecosystem, so how valuable is this product? A few thoughts….

    First of all, I think there’s a lot of merit to picking up this card for the excellent welcome bonus, which includes a lot of points. The card also has significant ongoing benefits. The card also doesn’t count toward the Chase 5/24 limit, which is nice. Given the value of the Atmos Rewards ecosystem, there’s no reason not to pick up this card, if eligible.

    It has been revealed that what about the long term value proposition of the card, though? If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency and don’t have elite status, the basic perks add up, including a first checked bag free, preferred boarding, a quarterly lounge pass, free points sharing, and more.

    However, I’d say there’s also merit to picking up one (or both) of the personal Atmos Rewards cards….

    It has been revealed that the $395 annual fee Atmos Rewards Summit Card is the most premium Atmos Rewards credit card. While it’s a personal card, I still think it’s worth highlighting, as it’s incredibly lucrative. I’d take it a step further, and say that it’s my favorite airline credit card.

    Among other things, the card racks up status points at the fastest rate, the card allows you to earn Global Companion Awards, offers Alaska Lounge passes, enables free points sharing, waives partner award booking fees, offers 3x points on foreign purchases, and much more.

    In a recent development, if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency, then getting this card is an absolute no-brainer. As I see it, the anniversary 25K-point Global Companion Award alone basically justifies the annual fee, and that states nothing of all the other amazing perks.

    According to recent reports, if you’re not set on an Atmos Rewards Business Card but want a dedicated business credit card that’s lucrative, there are some other great options that earn flexible points. Consider these if you want options for redeeming your rewards for more than just on Alaska, Hawaiian, and its partners:.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is an excellent business credit card that offers a massive welcome bonus and strong perks. The limited time welcome bonus of 90,000 Atmos Rewards points will come in handy for cardmembers, and is more than enough reason to get the card.

    In a recent development, if you don’t yet have this card and are eligible, I’d highly recommend applying. This is a card that many people don’t have, yet which offers lots of value and a great bonus.

The Andaz Gold Coast, located in sunny Queensland, will have 202 rooms and intends to "redefine coastal luxury through a distinctive blend of expressive Australian design and immersive experiences inspired by the people, places, and creative spirit of the Gold Coast," according to a statement from Hyatt.     Until then, Hilton fans should check into Rome Cavalieri, one of the most popular Waldorf Astoria hotels in the world.

    Industrial monitoring startup BrightAI closes $97M investment

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • BrightAI Inc., a startup that helps industrial companies detect malfunctioning equipment, has raised $97 million in funding.
    • According to recent reports, smith Point Capital led the Series A round.
    • According to recent reports, many industrial machinery malfunctions affect internal components that aren’t visible to an outside observer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 20:37 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

    BrightAI Inc., a startup that helps industrial companies detect malfunctioning equipment, has raised $97 million in funding.

    According to recent reports, smith Point Capital led the Series A round. BrightAI said in its Wednesday announcement of the deal that a number of other venture capital firms contributed as well. They were joined by GE Vernova Inc., an energy equipment organization that emerged from the 2024 split-up of General Electric Co.

    According to recent reports, many industrial machinery malfunctions affect internal components that aren’t visible to an outside observer. As a result, issues often go unnoticed until they cause a major disruption. Palo Alto, California-based BrightAI develops hardware and software tools that help customers spot issues earlier.

    The first component of the firm’s product portfolio is a collection of sensors called State Stickers. They’re small, rectangular devices with a ruggedized case and a long battery life. Technicians can attach them to industrial equipment to monitor for problems that can’t be detected visually.

    The motion of a machine’s internal components produces noise and  vibrations that tend to follow a specific pattern. If an industrial fan’s blades rotate 30 times per minute, it might give off a whooshing sound every two seconds. BrightAI’s State Stickers can detect when a machine diverges from its usual operating pattern.

    The sensors wirelessly transmit their measurements to a device called the Stateful AI Hub. It runs artificial intelligence models that analyze the data for signs of hardware failures. According to the firm, its models become more accurate as the number of sensors deployed at a site grows.

    BrightAI offers software that enables companies to augment the data from its sensors with drone footage. A utility, for  example, could use a BrightAI-powered drone to detect erosion at the top of an electric pole. The firm’s AI models automatically draw a square around damaged components to spare technicians the hassle of manually analyzing footage.

    Industry observers note that the manufacturer says that its software can also collect maintenance data in other ways. A BrightAI-powered drone can read the meters that are attached to assets such as data center coolant tanks to check their internal pressure. Furthermore, built-in support for infrared cameras enables the software to spot overheating equipment.

    The third core component of BrightAI’s product portfolio is an AI wearable. The Stateful Wearable, as it’s called, provides technicians with troubleshooting advice in the field. It also checks whether they follow safety guidelines during inspections and automatically turns maintenance data into reports.

    Sources indicate that “Our infrastructure is under more strain than it has ever been, and Physical AI has finally become reliable enough to work in the field,” remarked founder and Chief Executive Alex Hawkinson. “Bringing those two facts together is a once-in-a-generation opportunity.”.

    Sources indicate that brightAI says that its products monitor hundreds of thousands of industrial assets across 50,000 sites. Investor GE Vernova, which is also a customer, looks to expand its use of the manufacturer’s technology in connection with this week’s funding round. BrightAI, for its part, will use the capital to grow its international presence.

    Alaska Airlines Pulls 2 Nonstop Routes After Only 1 Year: See List Now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that alaska Airlines has dropped two routes from Hollywood Burbank Airport (BUR) barely a year after launching them.
    • It has been revealed that both routes had been suspended for the winter and were due to return as seasonal summer services in April 2027.
    • Alaska operated both routes with a daily flight, served by three-class, 76-seat Embraer E175s flown by SkyWest Airlines.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that alaska Airlines has dropped two routes from Hollywood Burbank Airport (BUR) barely a year after launching them. In a recent schedule update, the Seattle-based carrier removed all future flights between Burbank and Eugene Airport (EUG) and Redmond Municipal Airport (RDM) in Central Oregon.

    It has been revealed that both routes had been suspended for the winter and were due to return as seasonal summer services in April 2027. The two routes began on October 26, 2025, and operated year-round until the end of October 2026.

    Alaska operated both routes with a daily flight, served by three-class, 76-seat Embraer E175s flown by SkyWest Airlines. Burbank-Eugene covers 737 miles (1,186 km), while Burbank-Redmond is 714 miles (1,149 km). In August, Alaska suspended both routes for the winter, from November 1, 2026, to April 13, 2027, with daily flights scheduled to return for the summer.

    Alaska's Burbank-Oregon Traffic (October 2025–August 2026).

    However, according to schedule data from aviation analytics company Cirium, that plan has now been scrapped. Alaska has not explained the decision or announced any plans to bring either route back. The carrier took over both routes from Avelo Airlines, which had served them since May 2021 before closing its Burbank base. With Burbank-Pasco already dropped in April, none of the three former Avelo routes that Alaska took over at Burbank remain in its network.

    Industry observers note that US Department of Transportation (DOT) data indicates that the two routes performed almost identically between October 2025 and August 2026. Each carried an average of around 103 to 104 passengers per day across both directions, or about 52 passengers per flight. That left roughly 24 of the E175's 76 seats empty on an average flight, working out to an average load factor of around 69%. This is well below Alaska Air Group's network-wide average loads of 82.8% in the third quarter of 2026.

    Avelo opened its first base at Burbank in April 2021 and began flying to Eugene and Redmond the following month with Boeing 737s. However, in July 2025, the low-cost carrier declared it would close its Burbank base by early December, but later pushed its departure forward, operating its final Eugene and Redmond flights in October.

    Industry observers note that alaska revealed replacement flights in July 2025, as part of seven upcoming West Coast routes. It remarked Burbank would become its fifth nonstop destination from Eugene and its sixth from Redmond. Interestingly, Breeze Airways had also planned to compete, announcing twice-weekly Airbus A220 flights from Burbank to Eugene, Redmond, and Pasco starting in March 2026.

    Industry observers note that however, it scrapped all three routes in November 2025, before launching any flights. This left Alaska as the only airline offering nonstop flights between Burbank and both Oregon airports. The third former Avelo route, Burbank-Pasco, lasted just five months under Alaska, with service ending in May this year. San Francisco-Burbank was also cut in March 2026, leaving Alaska's Burbank network with year-round flights to Boise, Portland, Santa Rosa, and Seattle, plus a seasonal Honolulu service that began in May 2026.

    Alaska has continued to grow at Burbank even as the airport's overall traffic has fallen. Airport statistics show the carrier handled 956,077 passengers in 2025 — up 12.3% from 2024 — and 469,704 in the first half of 2026, an increase of 7%. Over the same periods, total airport traffic fell 5% to 6.22 million passengers in 2025, down from a record 6.55 million in 2024, and declined a further 8.6% in the first half of 2026.

    Southwest remains the airport's dominant carrier, handling 3.52 million passengers in 2025, representing over 56% of the market. Burbank also recently opened its upcoming $1.3 billion terminal in October. The project marks a major upgrade for the airport as it looks to modernize its facilities despite declining passenger numbers.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Atmos for Business is the small business rewards program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, and it runs parallel to the Atmos Rewards program (Atmos for Business used to be known as the EasyBiz program).
    • Industry observers note that most major US airlines have a small business rewards program, and the intent is to offer extra rewards when businesses book travel.
    • Industry observers note that along those lines, in light of the recent refresh of the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card (learn more), I think this program is worth a close look.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Atmos for Business is the small business rewards program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, and it runs parallel to the Atmos Rewards program (Atmos for Business used to be known as the EasyBiz program).

    Industry observers note that most major US airlines have a small business rewards program, and the intent is to offer extra rewards when businesses book travel. The good news is that even small businesses qualify for this, and it can really boost the rewards you earn.

    Industry observers note that along those lines, in light of the recent refresh of the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card (learn more), I think this program is worth a close look. Long story short, Atmos Rewards members could be earning up to 23.5x points per dollar spent on airfare. Based on my valuation of 1.5 cents per Atmos Rewards point, that’s the equivalent of a jaw dropping 35.25% return on eligible spending. That’s simply unrivaled.

    Atmos for Business is the self-managed business travel program by Alaska and Hawaiian, intended for small and medium sized businesses.

    The program is open to companies and organizations with at least $5,000 in annual travel spending, so if you’re a frequent flyer with the tech giant and have a small business, that’s not much of a hurdle. You can add an unlimited number of employees to your account, and all of their spending counts toward that requirement.

    Now, the terms suggest that you must have spent at least $5,000 or more on eligible Alaska and Hawaiian travel in the last 15 months, though in practice, that’s not directly enforced, best I can tell. After all, this is even intended to attract new businesses that may be looking to switch travel to Alaska or Hawaiian.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 20:48 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

    A bipartisan group of more than two dozen congressional lawmakers said today they’re forming a new AI Safety and Innovation Caucus to tackle the growing security risks posed by the advances in sophisticated artificial intelligence models.

    In a recent development, the lawmakers cited the July hack of Hugging Face Inc.’s servers by a team of autonomous AI agents developed by OpenAI Group PBC, which broke out of an isolated sandbox environment, as an example of these risks. They also pointed to another incident involving the now-public Anthropic PBC, which also reported that its agents escaped their testing environments to access third-party systems.

    In a recent development, these incidents have “underscored the need for Congress to better understand these risks and develop policy solutions,” mentioned Representative George Whitesides (D-California), a co-chair of the caucus. “As AI capabilities accelerate, so do the potential consequences of catastrophic misuse, loss of control over advanced systems and threats to national security.”.

    Sources indicate that whitesides (pictured) is co-chairing the caucus alongside Representatives Nathanial Moran (R-TX) and Don Beyer (D-Virginia). In a post on X, they stressed the need for bipartisan collaboration to create the basic policy guardrails for AI safety, citing the growing concerns of the American public.

    Does it feel like there's a latest tech or AI crisis every day? Recent headlines are raising serious concerns about our digital safety and security.

    Today, I'm joining @RepDonBeyer, @RepNateMoran, and over 20 of our colleagues to launch the bipartisan AI Safety and Innovation… pic.twitter.com/bhMyygy1J6.

    According to recent reports, — Rep. George Whitesides (@Rep_Whitesides) November 19, 2026.

    In a recent development, the 26-member caucus includes seven Republicans, which is a surprising number given that the White House administration under President Donald Trump has strongly opposed any heavy-handed regulation of the AI industry. The goal of the caucus is to identify “targeted solutions” that ensure AI remains under control without derailing innovation and threatening America’s lead in the industry.

    Whitesides remarked the lawmakers will focus on two things: proposing legislation to augment AI safety, and responding quickly to high-profile security incidents by gathering developers, independent experts and government officials to brief lawmakers and come up with solutions.

    In a recent development, “We want to be a conduit through which effective, responsible legislation can be refined and brought to the floor of the House,” Whitesides told Politico in an interview. He mentioned the group will work together to propose, provide feedback and endorse newly introduced AI legislation. He believes there’s an urgent need for this, because most other groups within the House are more focused on educating members or creating legislation within their own parties, he said.

    Another thing the caucus intends to do is to pursue relationships with outside AI experts who can help lawmakers to navigate complex policy decisions. It also wants to help raise public awareness around AI and its safety problems, and ensure members outside of relevant committees have the tools they need to contribute to upcoming legislation and debate.

    Recent findings suggest that in the recent midterm elections, Americans made it clear that AI is becoming a major problem for governance. Moreover, a recent survey revealed that 43% of Americans don’t trust either of the two major political parties to properly get a grip on AI safety, according to a one-pager that accompanied the press release.

    In a recent development, “Artificial intelligence affects every American, and it should not be a partisan problem,” Moran said. “This caucus gives us a place to find the areas of consensus, set partisanship aside and put smart, targeted policies in place so we can innovate while we keep people safe. Congress needs to be prepared.”.

    Media in Thailand is reporting on an incident that happened early this morning (Sunday, November 22, 2026), whereby a 46-year-old American tourist died at a hotel in Bangkok’s Phra Khanong area, after an altercation with a 39-year-old Italian man, who was reportedly an MMA fighter.

    According to the initial police report, the American had been arguing loudly with the hotel staff at the reception desk, for reasons that are unclear as of now. As an Italian hotel guest walked past him and attempted to enter an elevator, the American reportedly grabbed him and pulled him out.

    It has been revealed that the confrontation escalated, and turned into a physical struggle, during which the Italian man placed the American man in a chokehold, until he lost consciousness. Hotel staff called emergency services, and while first responders performed CPR, the American couldn’t be revived. Police also found an abrasion on the victim’s forehead.

    The Italian man remained at the scene, and told authorities that he had been acting in self-defense, after being attacked. Police took him into custody, and he potentially faces manslaughter charges, though the case is still being investigated.

    The hotel at which this incident happened hasn’t yet been named, but this occurred at Sukhumvit Soi 48 — there are several hotels in that area, with the biggest “brand name” property being a Ramada Plaza by Wyndham.

    What Are The World’s Tallest & Highest Hotels? The Answer Is Tricky…
