    Recent findings suggest that well stated. To the typical "premium" passenger that DL targets (who can't tell 763 from 123), DL is winning, regardless of avgeek nitpicking. Certainly in NYC, DL is reaching the crowd it targets very well.

    According to recent reports, wow, Daniel, you really came here to stir things up; first talking about flying economy and actually describing strategies to maximize it and now saying something positive about Delta. Surely, before you made your decision, you had your qtips out looking for crud in DL's 738 outlets, no? Your take is actually quite reasonable, not unlike how I see it, and in line with how the vast majority of actual customers - not those sucked into the aviation social media vortex - see it. DL doesn't have paid media influencers like a certain Chicago based airline and, like WN, has a reputation for being above average at what it does. addressing your key points, no one chooses DL because of their loyalty program. DL had the forethought to build a network over the past 20 years around the US' largest markets AND then to become the dominant carrier so that it has pricing control which works well when you are the largest carrier for corporate travel in the US - maybe the world. DL uses 763s to destinations from the NE that UA uses 757s; the DL 763 is a very competitive product compared to UA's old international 757s - and the few international 757s DL has left (which only fly domestic routes). DL's choice to wait to decide between the B787 and A350 and go with the 350/339 combo will reap DL benefits for years to come. As DL's first 20 A350-1000s are delivered over the next 2 years, DL will take a commanding position in the international arena with a widebody fleet that is more capable and efficient than any other US carriers'. as to the lounges, DL's Sky Clubs were far better than AA and UA's "standard" clubs for years and now their D1 lounges compete quite successfully with the best lounges in the world; as DL adds them to their core 4 domestic interior US hubs, they will be a force to be reckoned with in int'l travel. as to WiFI, let's be clear that the noise about Starlink comes from UA and its paid fan nut jobs that can't stand that UA lost the WiFi war to DL and UA is now competing with AA and WN to have fleetwide free high speed WIFI. With just 30% of its mainline fleet and only 9 widebodies with Starlink, UA is simply in the minor leagues compared to DL's 97% fleetwide availability of free high speed WiFI and global coverage which no other airline on the other offers as much of as DL. we could go on but anyone that reads this or any other aviation blog knows that the biggest reason I respect DL is because they operate the best run business in the airline industry and also are the consistently most profitable, taking a title that WN held for years. Lots of customers think finances and strategy don't matter to them and yet it is precisely DL's ability to think beyond other airlines that it ended up w/ the refinery which will save them somewhere around $750 million in fuel costs just this year, win the maintenance overhaul sales rights for every new generation engine in service, and created the most valuable relationship with a cobrand partner in the global industry. Those non-transportation distinctives allow DL to grow its network where it matters including in markets like BOS and SEA where it has displaced or taken a dent out of lower cost competitors as well as grow into major competitive markets with AA and UA including in NYC and LAX. With another SEA TPAC announcement seemingly imminent, DL seems set to continue to grow the one region where it has been weaker than it wanted and has historically been in the Pacific. DL has had a cadence of a new TPAC route about every 6 months and appears to be keeping up that pace. And DL has by far the best global partnership network in support of its own network; LHR, CDG, AMS and soon to be CPH are a wall between the US and the eastern hemisphere that no airline can beat. ICN is already the best hub airport in E. Asia and will only become more valuable as KE's acquisition of OZ is completed and DL and KE launch new US-E. Asia routes. AM and LA are simply unbeatable in combination with DL in serving the world. DL isn't perfect but it is one of the world's largest airlines just in passenger metrics but is also the highest revenue and highest market cap airline and has kept that up for years. It takes work for any business to stay at the top; it takes even more effort for a company to succeed both as a business and in the product it delivers. Few old industrial companies in highly competitive industries have done both as well as DL has done over the past decade plus. glad you look for my comments, Daniel, just as Ben has been accustomed to doing.

    Industry observers note that I don’t think Delta gets a bad rap, it’s just that it’s been on the downward trend for years now. In 2019, it was on track to compete with the true global heavyweights (I.e. rolling out amenity kits and courses meals in long haul economy). They were quicker to recover and better operationally than the rest of the US carrier. Now, they don’t clean up after IROPS nearly as well, they rolled back their ambitions during the pandemic and never picked them up again, their aging fleet of 767s is even more of a black eye than before, among other things. Their Delta One “refresh” is an example of what a mixed bag it’s become; nice sentiments and effort, but “simple comfort classics” sounds to me like they’re giving up on fine dining in the sky because it’s too expensive and/or they know they can’t execute. Meanwhile, United has been on the up and up the past few years. In the past, news stories about a new product or service would have been about Delta, now I see United more often. They’re building new lounges, and rolling out cabin upgrades and new planes too. Neither one is the clear winner like Delta was seven years ago, and it’s not like United has clearly surpassed Delta, but the trajectories are in contrast. I still fly mostly Delta because of my location and am not unhappy about it, but I will now look at United where feasible, in a way I wouldn’t have before. The less said about American the better.

    AI deals shrink to as little as 30 days as the data layer sets the pace

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Artificial intelligence has turned data infrastructure from a back-office purchase into the bottleneck that decides how fast GPUs pay off.
    • The storage industry’s longtime performance specialist sees that shift as its opening.
    • It has been revealed that “When you look at the data layer, performance in the data layer drives value.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 14:27 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

    Artificial intelligence has turned data infrastructure from a back-office purchase into the bottleneck that decides how fast GPUs pay off. As hyperscalers, neoclouds and enterprises race to expand their data layers, the way that infrastructure gets bought is changing just as fast.

    The storage industry’s longtime performance specialist sees that shift as its opening. DataDirect Networks Inc. built its reputation on scale and speed, and those traits now carry more weight in AI infrastructure, according to Kevin Delane (pictured), president and chief revenue officer of DDN.

    It has been revealed that “When you look at the data layer, performance in the data layer drives value. So yes, it has to be simple, it has to be reliable. Those are table stakes, but performance drives business value,” Delane said.

    Delane spoke with theCUBE Research’s Rebecca Knight and John Furrier at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how AI infrastructure sales cycles have grown more complex and faster, DDN’s tighter ecosystem work with partners such as Nvidia Corp. and Super Micro Computer Inc., and the company’s hiring for a direct, results-driven culture. (* Disclosure below.).

    It has been revealed that the way companies buy AI infrastructure has changed along with the technology. Deals at neocloud providers no longer go to a single enterprise buyer. They now involve the off-taker renting the capacity, the cloud operator and the integration software layer, Delane explained. Timelines have shrunk just as sharply, from six months to a year for a traditional enterprise sale to as little as 30 days.

    According to recent reports, “The sales cycle is more complex for sure. The speed is insane,” Delane noted. “Sometimes these things are 30 days and you have to be ready to turn things around and really work with your customers and partners quickly.”.

    It has been revealed that DDN is answering with tighter ecosystem work. Its decade-long partnership with Nvidia anchors the strategy, and joint offerings with Super Micro, such as the Enterprise AI HyperPOD, aim to replace a data center buildout with a ready-to-run AI stack. At SC26, DDN also introduced software-defined EXAScaler deployment to give enterprise AI customers more choice of hardware.

    “It takes the complexity out of it, allows an enterprise to set up an AI pod within 3 hours,” Delane remarked.

    Sources indicate that the performance case holds up in the public cloud too. On Google LLC’s Google Cloud, customers using DDN’s Managed Lustre service saw 70% better training performance and a 40% gain in overall GPU efficiency, Delane noted.

    DDN is growing threefold this year while adding only a few salespeople, leaning its hiring toward technical and implementation staff who can get customers up and running faster. Delane looks for grit and a fit with a direct, results-driven culture.

    “If people can fit that culture, want to come in, want to grow this firm to multiple billions, we have a place for them,” Delane said.

    #145502. Industry News: When To Use The Flight Attendant Call Button (And When To Skip It)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1357 w)

    Industry News: When To Use The Flight Attendant Call Button (And When To Skip It)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1357 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, to push the flight attendant call button, or not to push the flight attendant call button, that is the question.
    • Every airplane seat has a flight attendant call button, typically in the overhead console, right by the reading light and individual air nozzle (if the plane has those).
    • The flight attendant call button typically depicts a person with a tray, suggesting that the call button is intended for service.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, to push the flight attendant call button, or not to push the flight attendant call button, that is the question. I’ll share my take, and then I’m curious to hear how OMAAT readers feel. Let’s start with some background, and then we’ll discuss best practices….

    Every airplane seat has a flight attendant call button, typically in the overhead console, right by the reading light and individual air nozzle (if the plane has those). The flight attendant call button, is, as the name suggests, a way to call a flight attendant to your seat.

    The flight attendant call button typically depicts a person with a tray, suggesting that the call button is intended for service. However, that’s not how all flight attendants interpret it, so I want to talk about that in a bit more detail.

    Recent findings suggest that in most of the world, the flight attendant call button seems to work as intended. It’s a useful way to call over a flight attendant, whether you want a drink refill, or there’s some sort of an emergency.

    In a recent development, however, in the United States I’ve heard several flight attendants over the years announce that the call button is in fact the “emergency flight attendant call button,” advising passengers to only use it if absolutely necessary. Suffice to say that this kind of announcement isn’t approved by any airline.

    While people will often joke “well I’m happy you consider my drink request to be an emergency,” let’s talk about when it’s actually appropriate to use a flight attendant call button.

    Sources indicate that broadly speaking, it’s always appropriate to use the flight attendant call button for service in first & business class, especially on international airlines. You’re paying a premium for more service, and having an extra request on a long haul flight isn’t unreasonable.

    It has been revealed that I’ll take it a step further — at top airlines, crews generally prefer that you push the call button rather than going to the galley with your request. Foreign carriers typically have thick curtains between the galley and the cabin, and you generally shouldn’t try to go into the flight attendant’s “space” without permission. They’d much rather come to you. They might be putting on some makeup or eating a meal, and don’t want to be caught off guard. So absolutely push the flight attendant call button — it’s the courteous thing to do.

    I do want to mention just one caveat — try to be respectful of the overall service flow. For example, if a cabin has 50+ business class seats and the crew is doing service with a cart and is currently in the aisle, wait until they finish that round of service before pushing the call button again, unless there’s something you absolutely need.

    When it comes to using the call button, you can’t beat Emirates first class, where you can voice or video call the crew with any requests, without them even having to come to your seat.

    It’s also interesting to observe the cultural differences between airlines when it comes to service approaches. For example, in Singapore Airlines first class I generally don’t push the flight attendant call button, since even on a long haul flight, a crew member seems to pass through the cabin every 10-15 minutes throughout the flight. The service is just so proactive that I don’t find it necessary.

    In a recent development, cathay Pacific first class is exactly the opposite — the crews are spectacularly reactive. That might sound sarcastic, but it’s not. On Cathay Pacific you (hopefully) won’t see a flight attendant once between meal services without calling them, and that’s so that your privacy is maximized. But if you push the call button a flight attendant will cheerily appear within seconds.

    Sources indicate that of course those are both airlines known for great service. You have all kinds of other airlines where flight attendants make a habit of not passing through the cabin, and when they do they almost seem to look down, to avoid making eye contact.

    Sources indicate that using the flight attendant call button in economy is trickier. There’s nothing inherently wrong with it, but the staffing ratio in economy is different than in first & business class, and in many cases flight attendants have to walk a lot further to your seat. Also keep in mind that on long haul flights the crew has rest periods, reducing the staffing ratio even further.

    Personally I think there’s nothing wrong with using the call button in economy:.

    Recent findings suggest that that being said, in economy I also think it’s more reasonable to stretch your legs and go to the galley yourself. Generally there’s a small setup with snacks and drinks, at least on long haul flights, so you can help yourself to that. Furthermore, in my experience flight attendants are typically “sitting in the open” more in economy than in business or first class, given that the volume of requests is greater.

    Sources indicate that the above are my general thoughts, though is the story any different on airlines in the United States? This accounts for the fact that:.

    On US airlines I’m generally a little more hesitant to use the call button. I see what kind of a vibe the crew gives me. In general I don’t mind pushing the call button in international first & business class on a US airline, while I avoid it on domestic flights. If I get the sense that the crew takes issue with use of the call button, I of course won’t use it.

    Recent findings suggest that all airplane seats have individual flight attendant call buttons, though customs around using them seem to differ. In the United States, some flight attendants seem to think these buttons are just for emergencies, while outside the United States there are consistently no challenges with using them for service.

    Where do you stand on using the flight attendant call button, and what has your experience been?

Three hours into a seven hour flight, the meal service had still not been finished. It was the old cabin, which traps you unless you can fold the table tray. I didn't care if I hadn't been served dessert as yet I just wanted them to clear the dishes so at least I can get some shut eye. Would do it again if unfortunately, I was in the same situation. If there's a genuine reason, we should use it and not feel bad about it.

    My approach is simple: - no call buttons in short haul economy (I dont fly economy on long haul) - no hestation to use it in premium cabin, no matter the distance.

    I just flag one of the cabin crew when they walk down the aisle if I wanted something from the snack menu in Business or First.

    #145501. How to avoid petty theft while traveling

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • ⚡ Quick Read (129 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thepointsguy ↗ Open Full Page

    How to avoid petty theft while traveling

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (129 words, ⚡ Quick Read) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
  • Petty theft is a risk in many popular travel destinations, especially crowded tourist spots and public transportation hubs.
  • Travelers can reduce their vulnerability by minimizing valuables, blending in with locals and staying alert in busy areas.
  • Using theft-resistant bags, securing belongings and splitting up valuables are effective strategies to deter thieves.
  • Travel insurance may offer theft protection, but coverage varies, so reviewing your policy details is important.
  • Thieves often work in teams, creating distractions to target distracted travelers.

    Industry observers note that • In an unprecedented trilateral summit in China this week, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sat down with President Donald Trump. Ahead of the summit, Trump set no metrics for observers to judge its success. The summit cannot be said to have failed: It was not designed to achieve anything, and it didn’t. He reportedly sought commitments to nuclear disarmament from his Russian and Chinese counterparts, neither of whom had an incentive to agree to such limits. Putin sought to make the summit all about his war on Ukraine, but the Russian autocrat secured no meaningful promises on that front from Washington or Beijing. Only China, it seems, got what it wanted from the summit, which took place on its soil. The event allowed Xi to pretend to arbitrate the conflicts in which his great-power competitors are embroiled. The affair was not entirely unproductive, of course. It produced many joint statements of principle, which essentially state that all parties have agreed to keep talking.

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Siliconangle ↗ Open Full Page

    Inference pushes AI to smaller sites, making the data layer the deciding factor

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (974 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that inference is moving to the center of enterprise AI spending, and the AI data layer is emerging as the piece that decides whether those investments pay off.
    • According to recent reports, that shift is putting storage companies with roots in high-performance computing at the center of the AI conversation.
    • “As inference is off the charts in terms of utilization, the data layer is what makes a difference,” Bouzari mentioned.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 15:09 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that inference is moving to the center of enterprise AI spending, and the AI data layer is emerging as the piece that decides whether those investments pay off. As GPU costs climb and component shortages persist, the architecture behind AI is shifting from a handful of massive facilities toward a distributed web of smaller sites.

    According to recent reports, that shift is putting storage companies with roots in high-performance computing at the center of the AI conversation. Turning data into insight at an acceptable cost now depends on a resilient, secure data engine built for GPU efficiency, according to Alex Bouzari (pictured), co-founder and chief executive officer of DataDirect Networks Inc.

    “As inference is off the charts in terms of utilization, the data layer is what makes a difference,” Bouzari mentioned. “Costs are skyrocketing. GPUs are becoming more and more powerful, but also more and more expensive.”.

    Recent findings suggest that bouzari spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how inference, cost pressure and shortages are reshaping AI infrastructure. (* Disclosure below.).

    It has been revealed that the first wave of AI buildouts concentrated GPUs in large, power-hungry facilities. Inference changes that math because it needs to run close to owners and their data, Bouzari explained. Communities are also pushing back on giant monolithic data centers, he added.

    It has been revealed that “Now, what is happening with inference, you need to supplement that with smaller footprints. Let’s call them data centers, 1 megawatt, 2 megawatt, 5 megawatts. And those need to reside where the action is taking place, where the autonomous driving is happening, where physical AI is happening, where the sensor data is,” Bouzari stated.

    Connecting small pods back to large AI factories requires a different approach to data. DDN is building a software layer that spans many types of hardware, a direction reflected in its recent move to free its EXAScaler file system from DDN’s own hardware. The goal is to squeeze more use out of very expensive gear, according to Bouzari.

    “It is a software layer that needs to accommodate the different types of hardware because, look, the costs being so high, people want to be able to maximize the utilization over an extended period of time, just like it was in high-performance computing,” Bouzari said.

    It has been revealed that the scale of spending has changed dramatically. A couple hundred million dollars once funded the world’s fastest supercomputer but now buys 15 to 20 racks of equipment, Bouzari noted. Shortages of GPUs, memory and solid-state drives are colliding with tighter budget scrutiny.

    “On the one hand, you have budgetary constraints and the need to extract as much value as you can from your investment,” Bouzari stated. “On the other hand, you have the shortages. And so a data layer that can do a lot more with a lot less infrastructure, the smaller footprint is extremely valuable.”.

    That thinking extends into the enterprise. DDN’s Enterprise AI HyperPOD packages CPUs, GPUs, networking and storage into a rack that can drop into existing corporate sites with available power. Keeping the pod on-premises also gives companies tighter control over their data, Bouzari explained.

    “I think we’re entering an era where we will see a blossoming of smaller footprint pods being deployed in enterprises globally,” Bouzari remarked.

    Bouzari framed the AI data layer as the counterpart to accelerated compute, with Nvidia Corp. supplying the processing and DDN supplying the data. As inference and agents take over, the data side carries more weight, he mentioned: “You need both to make it successful. But the data engine, I think, is becoming increasingly vital as inference and agentic is really becoming the predominant way to utilize AI and get value out of it.”.

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov.
    • Saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen.
    • Democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    Saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen. Bernie Sanders said Wednesday that he would prioritize passing the universal health care proposal if he assumes the chairmanship of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee next year as expected.

    Democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters. And the idea could be buoyed by an influx of progressive lawmakers elected in the midterms.

    Sanders noted Medicare for All is gaining support from voters across the country who are looking to overhaul the American health care system as costs have soared. Democrats on the committee will move the legislation “as aggressively as we can, as rapidly as we can,” he said.

    Sources indicate that his version, introduced in April and referred to the Senate Finance Committee, would implement the universal health care system over four years. In the first year, the the age of Medicare eligibility would drop to 55 from 65, while coverage would expand to include dental, hearing and vision care. The bill would also provide coverage for eligible children during the first year.

    The age of eligibility would fall another 10 years in each of the following years until the fourth year, when coverage would be extended to all Americans.

    “If there has ever been a time in the modern history of our country . . . to address the crises facing working families, this is that time,” Sanders stated, noting that Democrats will have a 56-44 majority when the 120th Congress begins in January, the largest margin for either party in 16 years.

    Sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., along with nine other Senate Democrats, last week offered an alternative Medicare expansion plan, which would lower the eligibility to those ages 50 and up.

    Industry observers note that while who will be leading Senate Democrats is still an open question — Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Charles E. Schumer of New York, who has been the top Senate Democrat since 2017 — Sanders mentioned he is confident the Medicare for All bill will get to the Senate floor, “no matter who the [Senate majority] leader is.” Sanders previously expressed opposition to Schumer leading the conference.

    Asked about efforts to extend the Affordable Care Act enhanced subsidies, Sanders responded he’s “all in.” However, he added “the American people and elected officials understand the current health care system is broken.”.

    Subsidies that help enrollees pay for health care premiums on the ACA exchanges were expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, but these enhanced credits expired at the end of last year, raising costs for many who relied on them to help defray costs.

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, nominated on Wednesday to be speaker next year, previously outlined broader health care priorities such as extending the ACA tax credits and reversing Medicaid cuts enacted in Republicans' reconciliation package last year. When asked Tuesday how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that’s all part of an ongoing conversation.”.

    In a recent development, in addition to expanding Medicare coverage, Sanders reiterated his push to lower prescription drug prices. The Vermont lawmaker previously introduced legislation aimed at reducing the cost of brand name prescription drugs by linking domestic prices to international price benchmarks.

    To enact some of the agenda, Sanders may have to court Republicans.

    Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., noted last week that he prepares to serve as the top Republican on the HELP committee next year. Sanders said Wednesday that his likely GOP counterpart “has shown an enormous amount of courage in taking on Republican leadership year after year.”.

    Sanders added that although Paul may have a different viewpoint from himself on committee issues, he looks forward to finding common ground.

    Equifax cuts database firefighting after moving billing to Oracle on AWS

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, A multicloud strategy once meant deciding which workloads lived with which provider.
    • The credit bureau has moved nearly all of its on-premises data centers to the cloud and runs workloads across Amazon Web Services Inc., Google LLC’s Google Cloud and Oracle Corp.’s cloud infrastructure, according to Avinash Singh (pictured), vice president of technology services at Equifax.
    • “Their performance optimizer is so advanced that we don’t need to tune a single query,” Singh mentioned.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 15:53 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

    In a recent development, A multicloud strategy once meant deciding which workloads lived with which provider. Now database providers are moving into the clouds customers already use, and AI projects are raising the value of those migrations well beyond the back office.

    Equifax Inc. is a case in point. The credit bureau has moved nearly all of its on-premises data centers to the cloud and runs workloads across Amazon Web Services Inc., Google LLC’s Google Cloud and Oracle Corp.’s cloud infrastructure, according to Avinash Singh (pictured), vice president of technology services at Equifax.

    “Their performance optimizer is so advanced that we don’t need to tune a single query,” Singh mentioned. “Just think about that. Fifteen to 20 tickets per day turns into one to two tickets per month.”.

    Sources indicate that singh spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at Oracle AI World, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how a multicloud strategy is helping Equifax cut billing database tickets. (* Disclosure below.).

    According to recent reports, equifax’s global billing system runs on Oracle’s billing and revenue management software, rating and invoicing billions of transactions each month. The database behind it ran on Amazon Relational Database Service for Oracle until it hit a 65-terabyte ceiling. Oracle Autonomous AI Database on AWS, built on Exadata hardware, has room for petabytes of data inside the same cloud, as enterprise adoption accelerates. Because the application stack stayed on AWS, only the database service changed, Singh explained.

    “There is zero code writing because it is just about migrating the data from one database to another,” Singh stated. “We achieved this migration without any downtime.”.

    The results indicated up promptly after the system went live in April. Gathering database statistics on nearly 100 terabytes of data dropped from three to four days to three to four hours. After some configuration tuning, batch jobs that once handled 100 to 200 rows per transaction now process 15,000 to 30,000, according to Singh.

    In a recent development, “Our rating improved almost 200% to 300%,” Singh stated. “We are able to close our books way before what we have been closing.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 16:28 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

    An Anthropic PBC researcher claims to have used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, which is widely considered to be the most key open question in mathematics.

    Levent Alpöge revealed his discovery today on his personal website. Anthropic has not published an official announcement about the news. The company floated on the Nasdaq a day earlier in a landmark public offering that raised over $93 billion.

    Recent findings suggest that “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote in a four-page statement. “What I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.”.

    The Riemann hypothesis was proposed in the mid-1800s by its namesake, the mathematician Bernhard Riemann. It focuses on a specific mathematical function, the Riemann zeta function, that was discovered more than a century earlier. A function is similar to a software program: It takes a piece of data as input and outputs another piece of data. A function’s input and output can be numbers, other functions and many other mathematical objects.

    Sources indicate that the Riemann zeta function’s input and output are both complex numbers. Complex numbers share similarities with regular numbers, but also have many additional properties. When the inputs and outputs of the Riemann zeta function are visualized, they resemble a three-dimensional spiral.

    The Riemann hypothesis is concerned with a specific section of that 3D spiral. In that section, the complex numbers outputted by the Riemann zeta function all equal zero. The hypothesis argues that the inputs from which those outputs are derived all include the value ½.

    According to recent reports, the hypothesis is considered to be the most crucial open problem in mathematics for multiple reasons. The first is that although it focuses on a single, not overly complicated mathematical function, its implications extend to a far bigger topic: prime numbers. If the Riemann hypothesis is correct, a seemingly random aspect of prime numbers is in fact regulated by a pattern.

    According to recent reports, another factor behind the hypothesis’ importance is that hundreds of theorems operate on the assumption that it’s true. If the Riemann hypothesis is correct, those theorems are correct as well.

    Alpöge wrote that Claude proved not only the standard version of the Riemann hypothesis but also the so-called generalized variant. The latter conjecture argues that the Riemann hypothesis holds true for not only the Riemann zeta function but also certain other, similar functions. Alpöge believes that Claude will be capable of proving an even broader version of the hypothesis in the future.

    The researcher detailed that Claude’s proof runs for more than 250,000 pages. He has not yet released the paper. He did, however, publish a version of the proof written in Lean, a programming language used to verify mathematical results. The file contains millions of lines of code.

    Proofs implemented in Lean are essentially regular software programs. If a Lean program runs without crashing, the mathematical argument that it describes is correct. That makes it easier for mathematicians to verify newly published proofs.

    Citi AAdvantage Globe Card Review—I Applied For The Bonus, But The Flight Streak Perk Is Why I Like It

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 60 min read (11999 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~60 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog.
    • It has been revealed that I applied for the Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® [See rates and fees] when it launched because it was a fresh card I wanted to try up close and because it carried an initial bonus I hadn’t had yet.
    • Recent findings suggest that the reason I like having a Globe beyond the initial bonus is its Flight Streak benefit.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

    It has been revealed that I applied for the Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® [See rates and fees] when it launched because it was a fresh card I wanted to try up close and because it carried an initial bonus I hadn’t had yet. I wound up with two Globe cards, though: the one I applied for, and a second when my Barclays AAdvantage Aviator Silver card became a Globe.

    Recent findings suggest that the reason I like having a Globe beyond the initial bonus is its Flight Streak benefit. You can earn up to 15,000 additional Loyalty Points each year for American Airlines flights, without putting spending on the card. I already have the Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] and Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® [See rates and fees] cards for different reasons. Business is the best one for spending towards status, while Executive gives me lounge access and more bonus Loyalty Points. But Globe adds something neither of those provides.

    It has been revealed that at $350 a year, Citi AAdvantage Globe Card is worth considering both as your main American Airlines benefits card and as an addition to the cards you already have. But you need to value the benefits and having two Globes doesn’t double the Flight Streak bonus.

    The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card awards 5,000 Loyalty Points for every four qualifying American Airlines flight segments, up to three times per status qualification year. Qualifying Segments Flown Total Flight Streak Loyalty Points 4 5,000 8 10,000 12 15,000 These are segments, so a roundtrip with a connection each way is four flights. Three of those trips can generate the full bonus. Six nonstop roundtrips would do it, too. You don’t have to buy the tickets with your Globe card. You can use another card for its rewards or protections, or fly on a ticket your employer purchases, and still earn the bonus on your qualifying travel. The qualification year runs March 1 through the last day of February. Flights must be taken after you become a primary Globe cardmember. Qualifying flights are marketed or operated by American Airlines or American Eagle and ordinarily must earn AAdvantage miles. The terms expressly include American’s basic economy segments. Award flights don’t count. The benefit belongs to the primary cardmember. Adding authorized users doesn’t give each person their own Flight Streak bonus. Citi allows 8–10 weeks after qualifying flight segments post for the additional Loyalty Points to appear. (In practice it happens quickly.) These are points toward status, not another 15,000 miles you can spend on awards. For someone already flying American regularly, this can reduce how much additional spending or other earning they need to do to reach their next status level. There’s no requirement to divert $20,000 or $50,000 of purchases from a more rewarding card. I view the card as an inexpensive way to purchase Loyalty Points which are valuable both for earning status and for additional milestone rewards. Globe And Executive Work Together—Two Globes Don’t Double The Bonus When I analyzed Globe at launch, my criticism was that Citi wasn’t giving customers much reason to keep spending on it. From the customer’s perspective, though, that’s potentially a good thing. I earn the flight bonus while putting spend wherever it makes the most sense. The Executive card by contrast includes 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points at each of 50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000 Loyalty Points earned in a qualification year. Globe’s Flight Streak bonus can stack with that. Someone meeting all the requirements can earn up to 55,000 bonus Loyalty Points from the two products combined. The final Executive bonus requires reaching 240,000 Loyalty Points, so that maximum isn’t a shortcut to earning Executive Platinum from scratch. My second Citi AAdvantage Globe Card came from the April 2026 Barclays conversion. I initially wondered whether two accounts would generate two sets of flight bonuses. American subsequently confirmed to me that they wouldn’t. The Initial Bonus And Annual Fee The current offer for the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card is 60,000 AAdvantage miles after $4,000 in purchases within the first three months. The annual fee is $350, isn’t waived the first year, and there’s no additional charge for authorized users. There are no foreign transaction fees. The bonus restriction is specific to the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card: you can’t have received a latest account bonus on Globe within the past 48 months, and there’s also a restriction involving another Citi account with a recent bonus that you converted into Globe. Simply having the Executive or Business card doesn’t disqualify you. What You Earn When You Spend The card’s earning categories are: Eligible Purchases AAdvantage Miles Per Dollar Loyalty Points Per Dollar AAdvantage Hotels bookings 6 1 American Airlines purchases 3 1 Restaurants, including takeout and delivery 2 1 Eligible transit, including taxis, rideshares and public transit 2 1 Other purchases 1 1 Bonus categories increase redeemable miles, not Loyalty Points. A $500 eligible American Airlines purchase earns 1,500 miles and 500 Loyalty Points from the card, in addition to whatever the passenger earns for flying. The 6 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings are separate from the miles and Loyalty Points awarded for the hotel reservation itself. (Reserve Now, Pay Later bookings don’t qualify for the card’s 6-mile earning rate.) For my own spending, Executive already offers 4 miles per dollar on eligible American purchases (and at 4 points per dollar, I actually prefer my Chase Sapphire Reserve® [See rates and fees]) and 12 on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings. Globe’s Splurge Credit can give me a reason to charge a particular hotel purchase to it, but the regular earning rate doesn’t. For everyday purchases, one American mile and one Loyalty Point per dollar can make sense when you’re trying to reach a status threshold. Otherwise, there are better returns available. Holding Globe doesn’t obligate you to make it your everyday spending card. It’s a good card to have, not a daily spend driver outside of the quest for status. Four Admirals Club Passes Each Calendar Year Globe comes with four digital Admirals Club passes each calendar year. Each is valid for 24 hours after activation, including visits to multiple Admirals Clubs during that period. The access rules make these especially useful for an occasional traveler with children: Each adult needs a pass. Each adult using a pass can bring up to three children under 18. The primary cardmember must be present, including when using passes for adult companions. You need a same-day eligible American Airlines or oneworld boarding pass. Unused passes expire at the end of the calendar year. A couple traveling with two young children would use two passes for a travel day, rather than four. But you can’t give the passes to relatives traveling without you, and these aren’t Flagship Lounge passes or a full membership with partner lounge privileges. In my experience, the usual capacity restrictions on purchased one-day passes don’t apply to Globe passes. And just because you see a sign saying day passes aren’t being accepted doesn’t mean they aren’t being accepted – sometimes they just don’t take away the sign. American sells ordinary day passes for $79. That doesn’t make four Globe passes worth $316 to everyone. I already have Admirals Club membership through Executive, so I don’t assign these passes additional value for my own access. The Companion Certificate Doesn’t Require Annual Spending After renewing the card, starting in your second cardmembership year, you receive a certificate for one companion to travel on an eligible domestic roundtrip for $99 plus taxes and fees when you buy a qualifying Main Cabin roundtrip. However, this isn’t a certificate for any flight you want. It has fare inventory restrictions and restricted dates. You book through American Airlines Meeting Services, and travel generally must be within the contiguous 48 states on American or American Eagle. Residents of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands have exceptions allowing qualifying trips from home to the lower 48. It doesn’t cover basic economy or partner flights. The primary cardmember must travel. The account must remain open for a full billing cycle after the anniversary month, and Citi allows 8–10 weeks for the certificate to become available. The certificate is valid for 12 months from issuance, with booking and travel completed by its expiration. I’ve gotten good savings from Barclays companion certificates, so I don’t dismiss these. If the eligible companion ticket would otherwise cost $500, replacing that with $99 plus taxes can cover much of the annual fee. The Credits Are Worth What They Save You Citi advertises more than $750 in value. I wouldn’t start with that number, but several benefits overlap with what I already have, and others require purchases I wouldn’t otherwise make. Up to $100 annual Splurge Credit. Choose up to two eligible merchants at a time from AAdvantage Hotels, 1stDibs, Future Personal Training and Live Nation. Activate your selection at Citi’s Splurge Credit page before purchasing. This is $100 total (not $100 per merchant). Eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings are likely the most practical use for many readers. Up to $100 in annual inflight credits. Use the card for eligible purchases on domestic American Airlines or American Eagle flights. Food, drinks and eligible Wi-Fi purchases can qualify. This is less valuable when drinks are already included in your seat or status benefits, or when your flight has free Wi-Fi. Up to $240 annually with Turo. This is up to $30 per completed trip, so it takes eight trips to get the full amount. Link the card at Turo’s Globe page and pay with it directly; digital wallet payments don’t qualify. I wouldn’t assign this much value unless I were already using Turo regularly. Up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years. Useful if you need it, but I have plenty of other cards offering this reimbursement. My original reaction to the Splurge Credit was that it wasn’t worth much to me. I already have plenty of hotel credits. And an AAdvantage Hotels booking generally means giving up the hotel points, elite night credit and status benefits you’d receive by booking directly with a chain. I like the inflight credit myself now that American offers more food for purchase on more flights – I get one item free as an Executive Platinum member but I can buy sandwiches and snacks for my family. The calendar-year benefits also improve the first year. Open a card in November, and you can use available credits and passes before year-end and receive fresh allotments in January, before the next annual fee. Flight Streak resets in March. The companion certificate starts after renewal. Bags, Boarding And Other Benefits Of The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card The card provides a first checked bag free on qualifying domestic American Airlines itineraries for the primary cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation. Group 5 boarding also covers up to eight companions. You don’t have to pay for the tickets with Globe. Those can be valuable for someone without status, particularly a family traveling together. They add little for me because my existing status already provides better benefits. Your AAdvantage miles also don’t expire while you’re the primary holder of an eligible AAdvantage credit card. There’s also a 10% discount on eligible non-flight components of American Airlines Vacations packages booked through the designated Citi booking page. The travel and purchase protections include trip cancellation and interruption, trip delay, lost or damaged luggage, rental car coverage, extended warranty and purchase protection. Rental coverage is secondary in your country of residence. Citi Entertainment and Mastercard’s World Legend benefits add access to selected ticketing, dining and other experiences. I’ll Pay $350 To Keep The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card If you only want a checked bag and earlier boarding, Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] is cheaper. If you want regular Admirals Club access, Executive provides a membership for its $695 annual fee. Globe earns its place with the combination of flight bonuses, occasional lounge access and a companion certificate without an annual spending requirement. There’s a case for holding Globe alongside Executive for the additional Loyalty Points. Here’s how I’d look at renewal. If you get a real $100 of savings from the Splurge Credit, there’s $250 of annual fee left to justify through the flight bonus, companion certificate and other benefits. Earning all 15,000 Flight Streak Loyalty Points at that cost works out to about 1.67 cents per point before assigning any value to the remaining benefits. An extra 15,000 that gets you to the next status level is much more useful than points that leave you between thresholds. For someone flying at least 12 qualifying segments and pursuing American status, I think Globe is a strong addition even with another AAdvantage card. A $500 eligible American Airlines purchase earns 1,500 miles and 500 Loyalty Points from the card, in addition to whatever the passenger earns for flying. The 6 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings are separate from the miles and Loyalty Points awarded for the hotel reservation itself. (Reserve Now, Pay Later bookings don’t qualify for the card’s 6-mile earning rate.) For my own spending, Executive already offers 4 miles per dollar on eligible American purchases (and at 4 points per dollar, I actually prefer my Chase Sapphire Reserve® [See rates and fees]) and 12 on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings. Globe’s Splurge Credit can give me a reason to charge a particular hotel purchase to it, but the regular earning rate doesn’t. For everyday purchases, one American mile and one Loyalty Point per dollar can make sense when you’re trying to reach a status threshold. Otherwise, there are better returns available. Holding Globe doesn’t obligate you to make it your everyday spending card. It’s a good card to have, not a daily spend driver outside of the quest for status. Four Admirals Club Passes Each Calendar Year Globe comes with four digital Admirals Club passes each calendar year. Each is valid for 24 hours after activation, including visits to multiple Admirals Clubs during that period. The access rules make these especially useful for an occasional traveler with children: Each adult needs a pass. Each adult using a pass can bring up to three children under 18. The primary cardmember must be present, including when using passes for adult companions. You need a same-day eligible American Airlines or oneworld boarding pass. Unused passes expire at the end of the calendar year. A couple traveling with two young children would use two passes for a travel day, rather than four. But you can’t give the passes to relatives traveling without you, and these aren’t Flagship Lounge passes or a full membership with partner lounge privileges. In my experience, the usual capacity restrictions on purchased one-day passes don’t apply to Globe passes. And just because you see a sign saying day passes aren’t being accepted doesn’t mean they aren’t being accepted – sometimes they just don’t take away the sign. American sells ordinary day passes for $79. That doesn’t make four Globe passes worth $316 to everyone. I already have Admirals Club membership through Executive, so I don’t assign these passes additional value for my own access. The Companion Certificate Doesn’t Require Annual Spending After renewing the card, starting in your second cardmembership year, you receive a certificate for one companion to travel on an eligible domestic roundtrip for $99 plus taxes and fees when you buy a qualifying Main Cabin roundtrip. However, this isn’t a certificate for any flight you want. It has fare inventory restrictions and restricted dates. You book through American Airlines Meeting Services, and travel generally must be within the contiguous 48 states on American or American Eagle. Residents of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands have exceptions allowing qualifying trips from home to the lower 48. It doesn’t cover basic economy or partner flights. The primary cardmember must travel. The account must remain open for a full billing cycle after the anniversary month, and Citi allows 8–10 weeks for the certificate to become available. The certificate is valid for 12 months from issuance, with booking and travel completed by its expiration. I’ve gotten good savings from Barclays companion certificates, so I don’t dismiss these. If the eligible companion ticket would otherwise cost $500, replacing that with $99 plus taxes can cover much of the annual fee. The Credits Are Worth What They Save You Citi advertises more than $750 in value. I wouldn’t start with that number, but several benefits overlap with what I already have, and others require purchases I wouldn’t otherwise make. Up to $100 annual Splurge Credit. Choose up to two eligible merchants at a time from AAdvantage Hotels, 1stDibs, Future Personal Training and Live Nation. Activate your selection at Citi’s Splurge Credit page before purchasing. This is $100 total (not $100 per merchant). Eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings are likely the most practical use for many readers. Up to $100 in annual inflight credits. Use the card for eligible purchases on domestic American Airlines or American Eagle flights. Food, drinks and eligible Wi-Fi purchases can qualify. This is less valuable when drinks are already included in your seat or status benefits, or when your flight has free Wi-Fi. Up to $240 annually with Turo. This is up to $30 per completed trip, so it takes eight trips to get the full amount. Link the card at Turo’s Globe page and pay with it directly; digital wallet payments don’t qualify. I wouldn’t assign this much value unless I were already using Turo regularly. Up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years. Useful if you need it, but I have plenty of other cards offering this reimbursement. My original reaction to the Splurge Credit was that it wasn’t worth much to me. I already have plenty of hotel credits. And an AAdvantage Hotels booking generally means giving up the hotel points, elite night credit and status benefits you’d receive by booking directly with a chain. I like the inflight credit myself now that American offers more food for purchase on more flights – I get one item free as an Executive Platinum member but I can buy sandwiches and snacks for my family. The calendar-year benefits also improve the first year. Open a card in November, and you can use available credits and passes before year-end and receive fresh allotments in January, before the next annual fee. Flight Streak resets in March. The companion certificate starts after renewal. Bags, Boarding And Other Benefits Of The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card The card provides a first checked bag free on qualifying domestic American Airlines itineraries for the primary cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation. Group 5 boarding also covers up to eight companions. You don’t have to pay for the tickets with Globe. Those can be valuable for someone without status, particularly a family traveling together. They add little for me because my existing status already provides better benefits. Your AAdvantage miles also don’t expire while you’re the primary holder of an eligible AAdvantage credit card. There’s also a 10% discount on eligible non-flight components of American Airlines Vacations packages booked through the designated Citi booking page. The travel and purchase protections include trip cancellation and interruption, trip delay, lost or damaged luggage, rental car coverage, extended warranty and purchase protection. Rental coverage is secondary in your country of residence. Citi Entertainment and Mastercard’s World Legend benefits add access to selected ticketing, dining and other experiences. I’ll Pay $350 To Keep The Citi AAdvantage Globe Card If you only want a checked bag and earlier boarding, Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] is cheaper. If you want regular Admirals Club access, Executive provides a membership for its $695 annual fee. Globe earns its place with the combination of flight bonuses, occasional lounge access and a companion certificate without an annual spending requirement. There’s a case for holding Globe alongside Executive for the additional Loyalty Points. Here’s how I’d look at renewal. If you get a real $100 of savings from the Splurge Credit, there’s $250 of annual fee left to justify through the flight bonus, companion certificate and other benefits. Earning all 15,000 Flight Streak Loyalty Points at that cost works out to about 1.67 cents per point before assigning any value to the remaining benefits. An extra 15,000 that gets you to the next status level is much more useful than points that leave you between thresholds. For someone flying at least 12 qualifying segments and pursuing American status, I think Globe is a strong addition even with another AAdvantage card.     The current offer for the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card is 60,000 AAdvantage miles after $4,000 in purchases within the first three months. The annual fee is $350, isn’t waived the first year, and there’s no additional charge for authorized customers. There are no foreign transaction fees.

    According to recent reports, the bonus restriction is specific to the Citi AAdvantage Globe Card: you can’t have received a upcoming account bonus on Globe within the past 48 months, and there’s also a restriction involving another Citi account with a recent bonus that you converted into Globe. Simply having the Executive or Business card doesn’t disqualify you.

    Restored to Calder’s plan, the clouds are spinning again

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1162 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday.
    • The day after Alexander Calder presented his plan for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.
    • According to recent reports, fifty years later, Alexander S.C.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    The day after Alexander Calder presented his plan for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.

    According to recent reports, fifty years later, Alexander S.C. Rower felt a sense of awe as he stared up at his grandfather’s work, finally restored to what he had envisioned.

    “It’s totally phenomenal,” he noted, pointing up at the now-moving clouds as he spoke, spinning his finger around. “It’s not entertainment, but it’s trying to emulate naturalness, trying to emulate what nature would do.”.

    Industry observers note that it was a long time coming for Rower, who remembers traveling to the Capitol in his 20s for the original dedication of the Mountains and Clouds sculpture in 1987. The mobile portion stopped rotating as Calder intended in the 1990s, and it was ultimately removed in 2014 after being deemed unsafe by the Architect of the Capitol. Millions of dollars in private philanthropy later, Calder’s clouds are spinning again.

    According to recent reports, rower was back on the Hill on Wednesday for an event celebrating the restoration, joining Architect of the Capitol Thomas Austin, Sens. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., Angus King, I-Maine, and James Lankford, R-Okla., and the project’s donors. As the speakers addressed the crowd, the clouds began to speed up slightly. Onlookers gathered on the balconies overlooking the atrium and peeked through office windows. Attendees left with tote bags emblazoned with images of Calder’s art.

    According to Rower, who leads the Calder Foundation dedicated to preserving and interpreting his grandfather’s art, the mobile is rotating on a 15-hour cycle that is “totally variable.”.

    “It can go a little faster; it can go a little slower,” he said. “I told the team today that during lunchtime, I want it to speed up just a little bit because everyone’s going to lunch. There’ll be … a lot of activity passing through, and then right at 2:30, well, let’s make it go quieter.”.

    It was a labor of love for those involved, and not an inexpensive one. Jon and Kim Shirley funded the $12 million restoration. Because the pieces were so large, they were transported on an extra-wide load truck and driven at a speed of 35 miles per hour from Michigan.

    Sources indicate that “We had to call every senator or governor that we knew on that route, which went through seven states, to get permissions,” he remarked. “That was a huge thing to overcome, and it all happened over a weekend. So my wife was actually on the phone with a governor’s wife on Saturday evening. The next day, he called up his Department of Transportation and got a permit.”.

    Christian Quilici, who helped manage the project on behalf of the Shirleys and stated he serves as a liaison between the foundation and Congress, said the hardest part of the project was the size of it.

    “We had to tear the wall down on C Street, which nobody really thought of in the beginning,” he said. “Nobody got how big this was until it highlighted up on their doorstep.”.

    Recent findings suggest that quilici stated he spent years educating at least 30 different senators about the quest to reunite the mobile with the stationary mountains left behind. Some of the biggest champions were seated in the front row at Wednesday’s event, including Senate Democratic Whip Richard J. Durbin. Absent was Sen. Christopher S. Murphy, D-Conn., who has been away from the Capitol while recovering from a stroke but has been a supporter of the sculpture’s restoration for years, pressing former acting Architect of the Capitol Joseph DiPietro on it at a 2024 Senate Legislative Branch Appropriations budget hearing.

    “Is there any chance that before I leave the Senate, or at least before I die, we can get the clouds back up there?” Murphy said at the time.

    Padilla read a letter on Wednesday from Murphy, whose state was Calder’s home for much of his life.

    It has been revealed that “This statue is actually a statement on our democracy, that we have massive pieces of monumental art right in the middle of our most key and most iconic government buildings. To get this piece of art restored to how it was designed by the artist, well, that’s good for Connecticut. But I also like to think … it’s good for democracy too,” Murphy’s statement stated.

    The restoration was funded entirely by donations from the Shirleys, who are prominent Calder collectors, according to Rower.

    Recent findings suggest that “It’s very emotional to see the work completed after 10 years of us working so hard with the Architect of the Capitol and Calder Foundation. It’s a very overpowering, overwhelming emotion,” mentioned Kim Shirley.

    It has been revealed that in addition to helping fund the project, she’s a former Senate staffer who worked in Hart before Calder’s work was installed. Years after her time in the Senate was over, her husband Jon wanted to show her the sculpture, now filling the space she used to walk through every day.

    But when the two arrived, the clouds weren’t hanging from the ceiling like they were supposed to be. He called up Rower, who was a friend of his, and remarked he wanted to get them back to how Calder intended. On Wednesday, the three of them stood together in Hart, looking up.

    Technological and engineering advancements allowed for newer, lighter clouds to be built and be safe to hang from the ceiling.

    “Before it was like a bulb, it looked like a hoagie sandwich, and now it looks just really sharp, like a razor cutting through space, which was Calder’s intention,” Rower said.

    According to Rower, it involved laser-measuring the original model of Mountains and Clouds sitting in a glass case nearby in the Hart atrium. The latest clouds, he stated, are made of carbon fiber.

    “These are giant things up in the air, and they’re just so gentle and subtle,” he remarked.

    Younger Hill staffers don’t know a time with clouds. But for those who have spent decades in the building, it was a special moment to see them spin, as Lankford told the crowd.

    “I can’t tell you how many tour groups that I’ve walked through this building and I pointed to this, and I remarked it’s only half there, and would take them over to the little model that’s right over here, and say this is what it’s supposed to look like,” said the senator, a former Hill staffer himself.

    Standing under his grandfather’s sculpture, Rower found himself quoting the man responsible for it all.

    “I find that everything I do, if it is made for a particular spot, is more successful,” he remarked, gazing up at it.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    UPDATED 19:01 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

    It has been revealed that president Donald Trump today confirmed looks to impose a “tremendous tax” on U.S. companies that build data centers overseas.

    “We’re not allowing data centers to go into other countries because China will take all of them, and we’re not allowing that to happen,” Trump told reporters during a White House briefing.

    Sources indicate that that hints the plan may place particular emphasis on data centers optimized for artificial intelligence workloads. According to recent media reports, Chinese tech firms are using AI-optimized data centers in countries such as Malaysia to train their models. Such deals are designed to bypass U.S. restrictions on the export of advanced AI chips to China.

    In a recent development, if the tax initiative focuses specifically on AI data centers, it’s unclear what facilities would qualify. Cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services Inc. operate international data centers that include a significant number of graphics cards, but also run general-purpose workloads. Some of them were built before the advent of large language models.

    Last month, AWS confirmed prepares to invest 18 billion euros in Germany next year. A part of the capital has been earmarked for data center capacity. A few weeks earlier, Google LLC committed 13 billion euros to building computing infrastructure and supporting assets in Finland. A significant newly introduced tax on international data center projects may lead some industry players to revise their investment plans.

    In a recent development, if Trump’s proposed tax is not focused on AI-optimized data centers alone, it could have even broader implications for cloud providers. He indicated that he did not discuss the plan with White House officials before announcing it. According to the Associated Press, there’s currently no information on how the tax would be implemented.

    “We want them to build it here. If they won’t go in Texas or they won’t go in California, they’re going to go in West Virginia,” Trump said. “We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they’re great places.”.

    Recent findings suggest that during this month’s midterm elections, voters in multiple states approved ballot measures designed to limit data center construction. On Thursday, a bipartisan group of lawmakers formed a congressional caucus dedicated to tackling AI risks.

    Industry observers note that trump’s announcement of the data center tax plan comes a few days after the U.S. Commerce Department imposed upcoming restrictions on overseas AI facilities. The rules are designed to curb Chinese companies’ access to cutting-edge graphics cards.

    According to the Financial Times, at least two chipmakers have suspended some hardware shipments in response to the move. Nscale Global Holdings Ltd., a prominent neocloud, will reportedly have to secure a Commerce Department license to continue working with its largest customer.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that hyatt has signed up for another 10 years with Pepsi, covering more than 700 U.S. hotels. After Marriott finally decided to switch to Coca-Cola, Hyatt is sticking with the beverage that prompts a question nobody wants to hear: Is Pepsi okay? No, it isn’t. I rarely drink soda. When I do, I don’t want to waste it on Pepsi. The renewal revealed November 19, flagged by The Bulkhead Seat, doesn’t cover every Hyatt brand or every country. But the economics of choosing Pepsi make more sense once you realize that the person negotiating the contract isn’t the one that has to drink it. Which Hyatt Brands Are Covered, And Where Can You Get Coke? The agreement covers U.S. hotels in Hyatt’s Classics and Essentials portfolios. Translating Hyatt’s brand groupings: Portfolio Brands Classics Grand Hyatt, Hyatt Regency, Destination by Hyatt, Hyatt Centric, Hyatt Vacation Club, Hyatt Essentials Hyatt Place, Hyatt House, Hyatt Studios, Hyatt Select, Caption by Hyatt, Unscripted by Hyatt UrCove also belongs to Essentials, but its Chinese hotels aren’t covered by a U.S. agreement. The Luxury, Lifestyle and Inclusive Collection portfolios aren’t part of this deal. No one wants to show up at an Andaz or Park Hyatt and get told they can’t have a Coke. Alila, Thompson, The Standard, and Hyatt Ziva and Zilara are also outside the deal’s scope. Here are some hotels that have specifically listed Coke: Hotel Coca-Cola On The Menu Park Hyatt New York Room service lists Coke and Diet Coke Andaz Maui Meeting and event menus list Coke and Diet Coke Thompson Dallas Room service lists Coke and Diet Coke Alila Marea Beach Resort Encinitas Room service lists bottled Coke Pepsi Doesn’t Have To Be Your First Choice To Win The Business When I covered Marriott’s switch in April, Marriott told hotels that more than 70% of its guests favored the Coca-Cola portfolio. Hotels choose suppliers based on the total deal: product pricing, rebates, equipment, servicing, marketing support and sometimes direct payments. We can see how this works in a public contract. Fresno, California’s 2018 Pepsi agreement for its convention center offered a $20,000 annual sponsorship payment, a 25% vending commission, $3 rebates per case or gallon sold, bulk pricing and equipment maintenance in exchange for exclusive beverage rights. A hotel has a modestly captive audience. You’ve already booked the room, your conference is downstairs, or you’re sitting by the pool. You can buy a Coke elsewhere, but that takes effort. Some people accept Pepsi. Others choose something else. The hotel loses some beverage sales and creates some disappointment. But it still thinks it can come out ahead if its supplier prices and rebates are better and they aren’t seeing guests change their hotel bookings. In other words, the worse product can be more profitable to the hotel – or at least to Hyatt corporate. Here, Hyatt brings access to guests whose hotel decision usually turns on something other than soda. Pepsi doesn’t have to persuade all those guests that it tastes better (it doesn’t). Getting its products stocked on property can shift purchases without changing anyone’s preferences. The tests hadn’t captured how people would react to having their Coke taken away. The company could produce a drink that performed better in a test and still make customers furious by replacing the one they loved.
